title: Claire Saffitz Croissants (⅓ batch)
description: Claire Saffitz's croissants scaled to one-third (6 croissants). Butter block 113 g; roll to a 5-inch square, first roll 15x5 in, final 10x9 in trimmed to 9.5x9, cut three 3x9-inch strips into 6 triangles.
ingredients: 202 g all-purpose or bread flour, plus more for dusting
19 g unsalted butter, chilled, cut into small pieces
113 g unsalted European-style butter (butter block), chilled
instructions: Make the detrempe: mix flour, sugar, salt, yeast, water, milk, and the 19 g butter into a dough; chill.
Enclose the 113 g butter block and laminate with the classic turns, resting in the fridge between turns.
Roll to a 10x9-inch rectangle, trim to 9.5x9, and cut three 3x9-inch strips, then into 6 triangles.
Shape into croissants, proof until puffy, egg-wash with the yolk/cream mix, and bake until deep golden.

title: Pasta With Green Pea Sauce
description: Fusilli tossed with caramelized leeks and a bright blender sauce of green peas, mint, garlic and lemon, finished with pecorino. By Food52.

ingredients.original: 2 tablespoons (30ml, or more) fresh lemon juice
1 pound fusilli (or another short dried pasta shape)
1/3 cup (8g) coarsely chopped mint leaves, plus more for serving
1 cup (90g) finely grated Pecorino, plus more for serving

instructions: In a small pot over medium-low heat, cook the oil and garlic, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 minutes, until the garlic just begins to caramelize. Remove the pot from the heat.

Meanwhile, set a large pot of water over high heat. When the water is boiling, add the peas and cook for 2 minutes, then use a slotted spoon to transfer to a blender (we'll use that water to cook the pasta in just a bit).

To the blender, add the garlic and oil, mint, water, lemon juice, and salt; season with black pepper. Blend on high speed until a smooth purée forms. Taste and adjust with salt and lemon juice as needed.
Do Ahead: The purée, without the lemon juice, can be made 3 days ahead. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Add the lemon juice the day you're going to serve.

To prepare the leeks, remove the tough, dark green outer layers. Halve each leek lengthwise, keeping the root end intact. Rinse the leeks under cold running water, carefully removing all of the dirt and grit from the layers. Slice into half-moons about 1/2 inch wide; discard the root.

Bring the water used to cook the peas back to a boil. Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium heat, cook the leeks, oil, chili flakes, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the leeks are soft and just beginning to caramelize.

When the water is rapidly boiling, season with salt until the water tastes pleasantly salty, then cook the fusilli for 1 minute less than the package directions. Drain, reserving 1/2 cup of the pasta cooking liquid.
Add the pasta and the reserved pasta cooking liquid to the skillet with the leeks and toss to combine. (If your skillet isn't big enough, transfer back to the pasta pot.)

Add the pea purée and 1/3 cup of the mint to the pasta and heat over medium. Stir until the pasta is fully coated with the sauce, then add 1 cup of the Pecorino. Stir until the sauce is warm and clings to the fusilli. Taste and adjust the seasonings.
Divide the pasta among plates or bowls. Garnish with mint and a dusting of Pecorino.

title: Ricotta Dumplings with Leeks, Peas & Asparagus
description: Pillowy ricotta dumplings dropped into boiling water, then tossed with a buttery skillet of leeks, asparagus, peas and pea shoots. Finished with parsley or mint, cheese and olive oil.

ingredients.original: 2 tablespoons (30ml) olive oil, plus more for serving
1 large leek, white and light green parts only, thinly sliced
1 bunch asparagus, woody ends removed, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 cups (280g) shelled fresh or frozen peas
3 cups (60g) pea shoots or leaves, thick stems removed
1/4 cup (8g) parsley or mint leaves, for serving

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

Combine ricotta and eggs in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper and, using a large wooden or metal spoon, gently mix in the flour, taking care not to overmix (which could result in tough dumplings).

Meanwhile, heat butter and 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add leeks and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until leeks have softened completely and are starting to pick up some color, 5 to 8 minutes.

Add asparagus and peas to the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook, tossing occasionally, until asparagus is just tender and bright green, 2 to 4 minutes, depending on its thickness. Remove from heat while you cook the dumplings.

When the water is at a nice steady boil, drop the ricotta mixture into the pot by the heaping spoonful. (The dumplings will expand in the water, so make them slightly smaller than you'd like them to end up.) Be careful not to crowd the pot; cook the dumplings in batches if need be.

Once the dumplings rise to the top, let them boil until cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes. (You can always pull one out and cut it in half to test its doneness; the texture will go from dense and doughy to light and pillowy.)

As the dumplings finish cooking, use a slotted spoon to transfer them to the skillet with the peas and asparagus. Once they're all in there, give everything a quick toss over medium heat just to evenly coat the dumplings in the buttery sauce. Add pea shoots and toss just to wilt slightly.
Transfer to a large serving bowl or platter and top with parsley, cheese and more olive oil, if you like.

title: Pastéis de Nata (Portuguese Custard Tarts)
description: This pastéis de nata recipe makes as-close-to-authentic Portuguese custard tarts with a rich egg custard nestled in shatteringly crisp pastry. Tastes like home, even if you're not from Portugal.
ingredients: 2 cups minus 2 tablespoons (235g) all-purpose flour (plus more for the work surface)
2 sticks (8 oz) unsalted butter (room temperature, stirred until smooth)
instructions: In a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook, mix the 2 cups minus 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour, 1/4 teaspoon sea salt, and 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons cold water until a soft, pillowy dough forms that pulls away from the side of the bowl, about 30 seconds.
Generously flour a work surface and pat the dough into a 6-inch (15-cm) square using a pastry scraper. Flour the dough, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Roll the dough into an 18-inch (46-cm) square. As you work, use the scraper to lift the dough to make sure the underside isn't sticking to your work surface.

Brush the excess flour off the top of the dough, trim any uneven edges, and, using a small offset spatula, dot and then spread the left 2/3 portion of the dough with a little less than 1/3 of the 2 sticks (8 oz) unsalted butter being careful to leave a 1 inch (25 mm) plain border around the edge of the dough.

Neatly fold the unbuttered right 1/3 of the dough (using the pastry scraper to loosen it if it sticks) over the rest of the dough. Brush off any excess flour, then fold over the left 1/3 of the dough. Starting from the top, pat down the dough with your hand to release any air bubbles, and then pinch the edges of the dough to seal. Brush off any excess flour.

Turn the dough 90° to the left so the fold is facing you. Lift the dough and flour the work surface. Once again roll it out to an 18-inch (46-cm) square, then dot the left 2/3 of the dough with 1/3 of the butter and smear it over the dough. Fold the dough as directed in steps 4 and 5.

For the last rolling, turn the dough 90° to the left and roll out the dough to an 18-by-21-inch (46-by-53-cm) rectangle, with the shorter side facing you. Spread the remaining butter over the entire surface of the dough.

Using the spatula as an aid, lift the edge of dough closest to you and roll the dough away from you into a tight log, brushing the excess flour from the underside as you go. Trim the ends and cut the log in half. Wrap each piece in plastic wrap and chill for 2 hours or preferably overnight. (The pastry can be frozen for up to 3 months.)
In a medium bowl, whisk the 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and 1/4 cup of the milk (60 ml) until smooth.
Bring the 1 1/3 cups granulated sugar, 1 cinnamon stick, and 2/3 cup water to a boil in a small saucepan and cook until an instant-read thermometer registers 220°F (104°C). Do not stir.
Meanwhile, in another small saucepan, scald the remaining 1 cup milk (237 ml). Whisk the hot milk into the flour mixture.

Remove the cinnamon stick and then pour the sugar syrup in a thin stream into the hot milk-and-flour mixture, whisking briskly. Add the 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract and stir for a minute until very warm but not hot.

Whisk in the 6 large egg yolks, strain the mixture into a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and set aside. The custard will be thin; that is as it should be. (You can refrigerate the custard for up to 3 days.)
Place an oven rack in the top third position and crank the oven to 550°F (290°C) for at least 30 minutes. The oven needs this time to maintain this blazing hot temperature.

Remove a pastry log from the refrigerator and roll it back and forth on a lightly floured surface until it's about an inch (25 mm) in diameter and 16 inches (41 cm) long. Cut it into scant 3/4-inch (18-mm) pieces. Place 1 piece pastry dough, cut side down, in each well of a nonstick 12-cup mini-muffin pan (2-by-5/8-inch [50-by-15-mm] size). ☞ TESTER TIP: If using classic egg tart tins, cut the dough into generous 1-inch (25-mm) pieces. Allow the dough pieces to soften for several minutes until pliable.

Have a small cup of water nearby. Dip your thumbs in the water, then straight down into the middle of the dough spiral. Flatten it against the bottom of the cup to a thickness of about 1/16 inch (1.5 mm), then smooth the dough up the sides and create a raised lip about 1/8 inch (3 mm) above the pan. The pastry bottoms should be thinner than the tops.

Fill each cup 3/4 full with the cool custard. Bake the pastries until the edges of the dough are frilled and brown, about 8 to 9 minutes for the mini-muffin tins, 15 to 17 minutes for the classic tins.

Remove from the oven and allow the egg tarts to cool a few minutes in the pan, then transfer to a rack and cool until just warm. Sprinkle the pasteis generously with confectioners' sugar, then ground cinnamon and serve. Repeat with the remaining pastry and custard. These are best consumed the day they're made.

title: Crispy Masala Tofu With Lemon Rice and Raita
description: Craggy, hand-torn chunks of tofu are soaked in salted boiling water, tossed with cornstarch and garam masala, and cooked into shatteringly crispy morsels (no deep frying). The tofu is served with a streamlined South Indian lemon rice dressed with cashews, cilantro and turmeric, plus a tangy vegan tomato raita with a kick of green chile. Equally at home on a weeknight or at a small gathering.
ingredients: Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and freshly ground black pepper
2 teaspoons (10ml) neutral-flavored oil (such as canola oil or avocado oil)
1 big handful cilantro leaves and tender stems
¼ cup (20g) unsweetened shredded coconut (or use more cashews)
Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and freshly ground black pepper
3 tablespoons (45ml) neutral-flavored oil (such as canola or avocado oil)
Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Cook the rice: Bring 2 quarts of water to a boil in a medium saucepan and season with 2 teaspoons of salt. Add the rice and cook at a rapid simmer until tender but not soft or mushy, about 10 minutes. Drain, return the rice to its pot and cover for 5 minutes to dry. Alternatively, use your preferred method to cook the rice.

Soak the tofu: Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a small pot. Into a large heat-proof bowl, tear the tofu into chunks about 1-inch in size. Stir 1 tablespoon kosher salt (or half that, if using table or sea salt) into the boiling water until dissolved, then pour over the tofu. Cover and soak the tofu for 10 minutes, then gently drain. Spread the tofu out on a dish towel and dry the bowl to reuse.
While the rice cooks and tofu soaks, prep the lemon rice mix-ins: Juice the lemon, roughly chop the cashews and chop the cilantro. If there's time before the tofu and rice are done, start the raita.

Finish the lemon rice: Fluff the rice with a fork, then stir in 2 teaspoons of oil, the turmeric and a few pinches of salt and pepper to taste until evenly incorporated. Stir in 1½ tablespoons of the lemon juice, the cashews, cilantro and coconut, if using. Taste and adjust with more salt or lemon. Cover and keep warm.

Coat the tofu: Gently pat the tofu dry with a towel, then return it to its bowl. Sprinkle the tofu with the garam masala, cornstarch, a couple pinches of salt and a few grinds of pepper. Gently toss with a silicone spatula until well coated.

Cook the tofu (stovetop): Line a large plate with a few layers of paper towels. Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high until rippling, about 2 minutes. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook undisturbed until deeply golden brown and crisp on the bottom, 5 to 6 minutes. Flip the tofu (it's fine if some pieces stick together) and cook until browned on the second side, 3 to 5 minutes more. Transfer to the paper towels.

Cook the tofu (air fryer): Instead of pan-frying, reduce the oil to about 1 tablespoon and toss it with the coated tofu. Arrange the pieces in a single layer in the air-fryer basket (work in batches if crowded) and air-fry at 400°F (200°C) for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking or flipping halfway, until deeply golden and crispy.

While the tofu cooks, make the raita: Halve or quarter the tomatoes depending on size, or cut into bite-sized pieces. Finely chop the serrano chile, if using. In a bowl, stir together most of the tomatoes (reserving a few for garnish), the chile and yogurt. Season with salt and pepper to taste, and a squeeze of lemon, if desired.
Assemble: Divide the lemon rice, masala tofu and raita among bowls. Top with reserved tomatoes.

title: Saucy Peanut-Coconut Tofu
description: Pan-fried tofu simmered in a spiced coconut-peanut sauce with shallot, ginger, garlic, cumin, chile and turmeric, finished with lime. Served over rice with cilantro and jalapenos. A fast weeknight skillet dinner.
ingredients: 1 (14-oz.) package firm tofu, drained, patted dry, cut into 1/2" cubes
1 tsp. (2.5g) red chile powder or crushed red pepper flakes
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal (3g) or 1/2 tsp. Morton kosher salt
Cilantro leaves, thinly sliced jalapenos, steamed white rice, and lime wedges (for serving)
instructions: Heat 1 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Cook the tofu, turning once, until golden brown, 5-7 minutes. Transfer tofu to a plate.

Heat the remaining 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in the same skillet over medium. Cook the shallot, ginger, and garlic, stirring often, until the shallot is translucent and starting to brown around the edges, 5-7 minutes. Add the cumin, chile powder, and turmeric and cook, stirring, until the spices are fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the coconut cream, peanut butter, and honey; stir to combine. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thickened, about 5 minutes. Whisk in 1/2 cup water and the salt. Return the tofu to the skillet and simmer until heated through, about 2 minutes. Thin the sauce with up to 1/4 cup water if needed, stirring to combine. Taste and season with more salt if needed. Remove from heat and stir in the lime juice.
Scatter cilantro leaves and thinly sliced jalapenos over the saucy tofu. Serve with steamed white rice and lime wedges.
Do ahead: The saucy tofu (without cilantro) can be made 1 day ahead. Let cool, cover, and chill.

title: Melted Cabbage & Miso Pasta
description: A cozy linguine loosely based on Haluski: cabbage melted down with shallot, white wine, and white miso, finished with a heavy hand of parmesan and pasta water. By Emily Eggers (The Kitchen Table).

ingredients.original: 1/2 head of cabbage, halved and thinly sliced (around 430g or 15oz)
6 ounces linguine pasta, cooked to al dente
3/4 cup (180ml) reserved pasta water, more as needed

instructions: In a large pot, such as a dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced shallot and stir while cooking until they soften, about 2 minutes. On top of the shallots, add the sliced cabbage along with 1/2 tbsp kosher salt. Gently stir and allow the cabbage to steam and cook down.
Once the cabbage volume has reduced by about half, add the garlic powder and a few good cracks of black pepper. Stir and continue to cook over medium heat. The cabbage will continue to reduce.

When the cabbage has shrunk to a point where you can easily see parts of the bottom of your pot, add the white wine. Raise the heat slightly and stir until the wine cooks off. Lower heat to low. Add the white miso paste and stir until it is fully combined with the cabbage (you may want to add more water to help the miso combine).

Remove the pot from the heat. Add the cooked pasta along with the salted butter and approximately 1/4 cup of the pasta water. Grate on the parmesan cheese and allow it to sit for 1 minute to begin melting. Add another splash of pasta water on top of the cheese, then stir heavily to combine until the cheese and butter are fully melted. Taste and add more salt and pepper as desired. Add more pasta water as needed and discard what is unused.

Once the cabbage forms into a sauce with pasta water and cheese, serve the pasta hot on a plate, scooping more cabbage on top of the plated pasta. Garnish with more grated parmesan, black pepper, a squeeze of lemon, and finely chopped parsley.
Tip: Heavily salt the pasta cooking water; it adds flavor and gives the pasta water the right texture.
Tip: Good parmesan tends to clump when heated. Add it only after the heat is off, and use pasta water to help it melt.

Notes / substitutions: You can use another kind of miso, or omit miso and add extra parmesan plus a splash of soy sauce or tamari. Any pasta shape works, but avoid very thin or small shapes. Pecorino works in place of parmesan.

title: One-pan salmon and broccoli bake
description: For a healthy no-fuss dinner, try this simple one-pan salmon and broccoli bake.

ingredients.original: 4 green shallots, trimmed, thinly sliced, plus extra, to serve
1 long fresh red chilli, thinly sliced, plus extra, to serve
500g broccoli or brussels or asparagus, cut into florets

instructions: Combine the shallot, garlic, chilli, ginger, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil  and butter in a large glass or ceramic dish.
Preheat oven to 200C/ 180C fan forced. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place the salmon fillets in the centre of the tray and the vegetables around it and drizzle with the marinade.
Roast for a further 12-15 minutes or until the salmon is cooked through. Sprinkle with the extra green shallot and chilli. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Spicy basil chicken stir-fry
description: A fast, savory ground-chicken stir-fry with shallots, basil, oyster sauce, and hot chili paste.

ingredients.original: 1 lb. ground chicken (454 g ground chicken)
4 Tbsp. vegetable oil, divided (60 ml vegetable oil, divided)
¼ tsp. (1.5g) kosher salt, plus more
¼ cup oyster sauce (60 ml oyster sauce)
3 Tbsp. hot chili paste (45 ml hot chili paste)
1 Tbsp. fish sauce (15 ml fish sauce)
2 tsp. brown sugar (8 g brown sugar)
6 oz. basil leaves (170 g basil leaves)

instructions: Stir the ground chicken, 1 Tbsp vegetable oil, baking soda, salt, and 2 Tbsp water until smooth. Set aside.
Stir together the oyster sauce, chili paste, fish sauce, and brown sugar.
Cook the shallots in the remaining oil until softened and golden.
Add the chicken and cook until beginning to set. Break it up, add the sauce, and cook until the sauce clings to the meat.
Add the basil and toss until wilted. Taste and season with salt.
Serve with steamed rice and lime wedges.

title: One-pot Hainanese chicken rice
description: An easy version of the classic Hainanese chicken rice, this one-pot recipe is very simple to make. You can cook it in a regular pot, an instant pot or a rice cooker.
ingredients: 4 pieces chicken thighs, skin on (about 180g/6.3oz each (see note 1))
1 ½ cups (310g) jasmine rice, or short grain white rice
cucumber, sliced (or blanched green vegetables, such as Bok Choy, spinach, etc.)
instructions: Marinate the chicken:
Put the chicken thighs into a bowl then sprinkle with salt and white pepper. Rub to evenly distribute. Leave to marinate for 10 minutes or so.
Cook the rice and chicken:
Rinse the rice with cold water then drain well. Set aside.

Heat oil in a pot over medium heat on a stove (see note 2 & 3 if using an Instant Pot or a ice cooker). Add chopped scallions, minced ginger and minced garlic. Fry until fragrant (do not burn). Scoop out about ⅔ of the aromatic to a small bowl for later use.

Put in the drained rice and fry for 30 seconds or so. Add 2 cups of water and ¼ teaspoon of salt (see note 4). Use a spatula to scrape the bottom to loosen any grains stuck to the pot. Place the marinated chicken pieces on top of the rice without overlapping.
Leave to cook uncovered until the water starts boiling very gently. Put on a tight lid and turn the heat to the lowest. Leave to cook for 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat when the time is up. Let it sit for another 10 minutes (see note 1). Remember not to open the lid during the cooking and resting process.
Serve the dish:
Take out the chicken thighs. Remove the centre bones. Then slice them into bite-sized strips.
Put the rice onto individual serving plates. Place the chicken on the side, along with cucumber slices.
Add light soy sauce, lime juice, sesame oil and fresh chilli (optional) to the fried aromatics you saved earlier. Serve it as a dipping sauce or pour it over the chicken.

title: Pumpkin Cream Cheese Muffins (Starbucks Copycat)
description: These ultra soft, moist and fluffy pumpkin muffins may be the best I've ever had! They are so flavorful with the perfect amount of spice and with the softest texture. They're filled with a bit of slightly sweetened cream cheese like a little bite of cheesecake in the middle, similar to those muffins

ingredients.original: ½ cup (110g) packed light brown sugar
½ cup plus 2 tbsp (125g) granulated sugar

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a standard 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners. Here are parchment paper liners that I like to use for these muffins as they won't stick at all to these ones.
Make the pumpkin muffin batter. Combine pumpkin puree and both sugars in a large bowl and whisk until smooth and glossy. Add eggs, oil and vanilla and whisk to combine.

Combine flour, pumpkin spice, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a medium bowl and whisk to blend evenly. Add dry ingredients to the pumpkin mixture and start to fold them in but before it is all incorporated, add the milk and fold it in until the batter is evenly combined. It may be a tiny bit lumpy but as long as there are no flour pockets, then it’s fine. Cover the bowl and let the batter rest on the counter for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the cream cheese filling. Combine soft cream cheese, sugar, flour and vanilla in a small bowl and beat with an electric hand mixer or use a wooden spoon to blend until smooth. Add milk and mix until combined and smooth. Transfer the filling to a small piping bag or a zip-top bag.

Use a 2 oz scoop to divide batter evenly among prepared muffin cups, filling them to the rim. Snip the tip off of the piping bag (or the corner of the zip top bag) and place it into the center of the batter. It doesn’t need to be deep into the batter – it only needs to be about ¼ inch deep from the surface so the cream cheese shows at the top. Press down to squeeze, pulling up slowly in a circular motion to make a little swirl at the top to fill out about 1-inch diameter circle at the surface of the batter so you see it nicely. You will use all of the filling for the 12 muffins, and it will be about ½ tablespoon of filling per muffin. If you have any excess batter feel free to push the tip back into the center of the muffin batter and squeeze some remainder throughout each. Sprinkle chopped pumpkin seeds over the pumpkin batter (around and not over the cream cheese filling), pressing in slightly.

Bake at 425℉ for 5 minutes. Then, turn the oven down to 350℉. Bake for another 12-15 minutes until they feel firm when pressed and a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let cool for 5 minutes before transferring muffins individually to the rack to finish cooling.

title: Chocolate Candied Pecan Cookies
description: Buttery cookies with chocolate and candied pecans
instructions: Cream together butter, sugar, and brown sugar
Add egg and mix well
Mix together flour, salt, baking powder, and vanilla
Combine wet and dry ingredients
Fold in chocolate and candied pecans
Scoop onto baking sheet and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 10-12 minutes until golden

title: Montelimar Nougat
description: Soft white honey nougat aerated with whipped egg whites and loaded with roasted almonds and pistachios.
instructions: Roast the almonds 15 minutes at 150C and dry the pistachios 5 minutes at 110C.
Bring the water and sugar to a boil, add the glucose and cook to 155C.
When the sugar reaches 110C, cook the honey to 125C.
Whip the egg whites, pour in the honey then the cooked syrup, whip about a minute then switch to the paddle.
Dry the nougat with a blowtorch to the desired texture, add the melted cocoa butter and mix.
Fold in the hot nuts, smooth into a greased 20x20cm frame and cool away from moisture.

title: Œuf Mendiant
description: A molded dark chocolate showpiece egg with its seam masked by caramelized nuts, candied citrus peel and pistachios.
instructions: Melt and temper the dark chocolate, mold two 12.5cm half-egg molds and a 6cm half-sphere, crystallize at 17C.
Cook the water and sugar to 115C, add the almonds and hazelnuts and cook until the sugar crystallizes then caramelizes, add cocoa butter, pour out and separate the nuts.
Melt and temper 50 g dark chocolate, add the kirsch and mix until thickened, use immediately.
Assemble the two half-eggs and stick the egg onto the half-sphere base.
With the thickened chocolate, stick the caramelized nuts, candied orange and lemon peels and pistachios over the seam to cover it completely.

title: Pain aux Ingredients
description: A savory ficelle bread made on fermented dough and autolyse with delayed proofing, garnished with Comte, bacon or chorizo (nutrition based on the Comte variant).
ingredients: Chorizo variant: 285 g chorizo plus 38 g water
instructions: Autolyse: combine the flour and water (at base temperature 56-60 C) in the bowl, knead 1 minute on 1st speed and rest 30 to 60 minutes.
Add the yeast, fermented dough and salt; knead 3 minutes on 1st speed then 3 minutes on 2nd speed.
Add the bassinage water in a thin stream at the end of 2nd speed.
Add the diced, tempered garnish (Comte, bacon or chorizo) on 1st speed; final dough temperature 24 C.
First proof: 45 minutes at room temperature then 12 to 18 hours at 4 C.
Divide into 180 g ficelles, roll lightly into ovals and rest 45 minutes to 1 hour, then shape.
Second proof about 1h15 at 20 C.
Flour and score, then load at 250 C and bake 15 minutes at 230 C (falling heat) in a deck oven.

title: Chocolate and Caramel Bar
description: Molded dark chocolate bars layered with soft caramel, almond nougatine and a whipped caramel ganache, then sealed.
instructions: Melt and temper the bronze and milk cocoa butters to 29C, spray the mold in the desired decor and crystallize.
Melt and temper the dark chocolate, line the mold and crystallize at 17C.
For the nougatine, melt the sugar, butter and glucose, add sliced almonds, spread thin, bake 10 minutes at 180C and cut into 16x6cm rectangles.
For the soft caramel, make a dark caramel with sugar and glucose, deglaze with salted cream, recook to 107C, add butter and blend, cool to 29C and fill the bars with 5mm caramel.
For the whipped ganache, make a dark caramel with sugar, deglaze with butter then salted cream, pour over the chopped chocolates and Vegetaline, blend and crystallize 3 hours at 4C.
Whip the ganache briefly, fill the bars to 3mm from the edge, set a nougatine rectangle and crystallize at 17C.
Seal with tempered dark chocolate, set 1 hour at 17C and unmold.

title: Baba au Rhum
description: Light yeasted baba cakes soaked in vanilla-citrus rum syrup, glazed and topped with vanilla Chantilly cream.
ingredients: Baba dough: 70 g butter, 10 g semi-skimmed milk, 10 g honey, 9 g fresh yeast, 250 g whole eggs, 2 g salt, 200 g pastry wheat flour T65
Syrup: 1000 g water, 400 g caster sugar, 1 orange, 1 lemon, 1 vanilla pod, 50 g brown rum
Vanilla Chantilly cream: 250 g liquid cream 35%, 25 g caster sugar, 1 g vanilla powder
Finishing: 250 g neutral hot-use glaze, 100 g brown rum, 1 g vanilla powder
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the milk and half the eggs, add butter, honey, salt and flour, then knead with the hook until a glutinous network forms.
Add the remaining eggs gradually and knead until the dough comes off the sides of the bowl.
Rest 30 minutes at room temperature, punch down, then pipe into buttered molds filled halfway; let rise 35 minutes at 27C.
Bake 12 minutes at 175C, unmold, then bake again 12 minutes at 165C.
For the syrup, boil water and sugar, add orange and lemon zest and scraped vanilla pod, simmer and infuse; strain, cool to 60C and add the rum.
Dip the babas in the 60C syrup until fully soaked, then drain.
Whip the cream with the vanilla sugar to a Chantilly texture.
Glaze the babas, place in cups, drizzle the centers with rum, pipe a Chantilly rosace with a star tip and dust with vanilla powder.

title: Brioche Cocktail Fruits Rouges
description: Individual brioche discs edged with almonds, baked around a frozen red-fruit insert and finished with glaze, pistachios and fresh berries.
ingredients: Brioche dough: 110 g pastry wheat flour T65, 110 g strong wheat flour, 5 g salt, 25 g caster sugar, 11 g fresh yeast, 132 g whole eggs, 110 g butter
Red fruit cocktail: 200 g frozen red fruits mix, 60 g caster sugar, 10 g cornstarch, 5 g kirsch
Baking: 35 g egg yolks, 15 g semi-skimmed milk, 100 g slivered almonds, 50 g icing sugar
Finishing: 70 g cold-use neutral glaze, 10 g chopped pistachios, 50 g raspberries, 40 g strawberries, 30 g blueberries
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the eggs, add flours, salt and sugar, and knead with the hook 3 minutes on speed 1 then 5-6 minutes on speed 2 until a glutinous network forms.
Add cold butter gradually and knead on speed 1 until the dough comes off the bowl (end temperature 25C).
First proof 1 hour at room temperature then chill (or 30-40 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Divide into 50 g pieces, roll, chill 30 minutes at 4C, then roll into 10 cm discs and proof 2 hours at 25C.
For the insert, heat the red fruits, add sugar mixed with cornstarch, boil until thick, then fill 6 cm silicone molds 1.5 cm deep and freeze.
Eggwash the discs, sprinkle the rim with slivered almonds, dust with icing sugar, press an insert into the center and bake 10 minutes at 150C.
Glaze the insert, sprinkle chopped pistachios and decorate with a glazed strawberry quarter, a raspberry and a blueberry.

title: Pain au Lait
description: A soft enriched French milk bread shaped as navettes or braids, glazed and topped with pearl sugar.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the eggs and milk at base temperature (46-50 C), then add the flour, salt and sugar.
Knead with the hook 3 minutes on 1st speed then 5-6 minutes on 2nd speed until a gluten network develops.
Add the cold butter and knead on 1st speed about 10 minutes until the dough comes off the bowl; final temperature 25 C.
First proof: 1 hour at room temperature then cool quickly (or 30-40 minutes at room temperature then 12 hours at 4 C).
Shape into 60 g navettes or 1-branch braids, or 300 g 3-branch braids (3 x 100 g).
Second proof: 1h30 at 26 C for navettes, 2 hours for 3-branch braids.
Egg wash, snip navettes with scissors, sprinkle with pearl sugar.
Bake in a fan oven: navettes 10 minutes at 160 C; 3-branch braids 10 minutes at 150 C plus 10 minutes at 135 C.

title: Financiers
description: Small brown-butter almond cakes topped with raspberries, pistachios, or slivered almonds.
ingredients: Batter: 80 g butter, 14 g invert sugar, 55 g pastry wheat flour T65, 145 g icing sugar, 55 g almond powder, 150 g egg whites, 2 g baking powder, 1 g salt
Finishing and baking: 15 g butter, 20 g frozen raspberries, 20 g pistachios, 20 g slivered almonds
instructions: Cook the butter until brown, then strain it over the invert sugar and mix.
Sift and mix the flour, icing sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add the tempered egg whites and mix without whipping.
Stir in the brown butter and invert sugar, then smooth.
Let set 12 hours at 4C.
Using a 10 mm round tip, fill the buttered financier molds with batter.
Top as desired with raspberries, pistachios or slivered almonds.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes at 180C.

title: Pain Courant
description: A classic French white bread made on fermented dough with intensive kneading (1750 g dough; portioned here as 5 x 350 g batards or baguettes).
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the water at base temperature (48-52 C), then add the flour, water and fermented dough.
Knead 3 minutes on 1st speed then 4 minutes on 2nd speed.
Add the salt and knead 3 minutes on 2nd speed; final dough temperature 23 C.
First proof 15 minutes at room temperature.
Divide (breads 550 g, batards and baguettes 350 g, ficelles 175 g, buns 70-80 g), roll into ovals and rest 15 minutes, then shape.
Second proof 2 hours at 20 C.
Score, load into a deck oven at 250 C and bake at 230 C (falling heat): breads and batards 25 minutes, baguettes 18 minutes, ficelles 15 minutes, buns 12 minutes.

title: Pate de Fruit Framboise Abricot
description: Set fruit jellies in raspberry and apricot flavors, cooked with yellow pectin and glucose and cut into sugared cubes (each flavor makes one 20x20 cm frame; estimated at 36 cubes per frame).
instructions: Make the acid solution: bring the water to a simmer, add the citric acid and stir until dissolved, then seal tightly.
Heat the fruit puree to 40 C, then add the pectin premixed with the 80 g of sugar and bring to a boil while whisking.
Gradually add the 400 g of sugar, then the glucose, keeping it at a boil.
Cook to 74 Brix or 105 C while whisking.
Add the acid solution, mix and immediately pour into the frame.
Once set, cut into cubes and roll in caster sugar. Repeat for each flavor (raspberry, apricot).

title: Esquimaux Fraise Vanille (Vanilla & Strawberry Popsicles)
description: Molded popsicles layering vanilla ice cream and strawberry sorbet, dipped in a crunchy white chocolate and almond coating.
ingredients: Vanilla ice cream: 400 g whole milk
Vanilla ice cream: 65 g powdered milk 0%
Vanilla ice cream: 160 g caster sugar
Vanilla ice cream: 60 g powdered glucose
Vanilla ice cream: 185 g liquid cream 35%
Vanilla ice cream: 75 g egg yolks
Vanilla ice cream: 3 g glycerol monostearate
Crunchy coating: 150 g Opalys white chocolate
instructions: Strawberry sorbet: heat the water; at 30C add the caster sugar (reserving a little for the stabilizer) and the atomized glucose and mix well.
At 45C add the stabilizer premixed with the reserved sugar; cook to 85C and blend with a hand blender.
Cool quickly to 4C and mature 12 hours at 4C; add the hulled strawberries, blend again, churn and hold at -18C.
Vanilla ice cream: heat the milk, scraped vanilla pod and milk powder; at 30C add the sugar (reserving a little) and glucose.
At 35C add the cream, at 40C add the yolks, at 45C add the stabilizer, monostearate and reserved sugar; cook to 85C, blend and return the pod.
Cool to 4C, mature 12 hours, remove the pod, blend, churn and hold at -18C.
Crunchy coating: mix the chocolate melted at 45C with the grapeseed oil, roasted chopped almonds and scraped vanilla; use at 35C.
Half-fill popsicle molds with vanilla ice cream and finish with strawberry sorbet; insert a stick, smooth flush and freeze.
Dip the popsicles in the tempered crunchy coating at 30-35C.

title: Gâteau Basque Glacé (Frozen Gâteau Basque)
description: A frozen take on the Basque cake with a baked Basque shortbread base, morello cherry sorbet insert and almond parfait, sprayed with neutral glaze.
ingredients: Morello cherry sorbet: 96 g caster sugar
Morello cherry sorbet: 40 g powdered glucose
Morello cherry sorbet: 250 g frozen morello cherries
Basque shortbread: 155 g pastry wheat flour T65
Neutral spray glaze: 130 g caster sugar
Neutral spray glaze: 300 g glucose syrup DE38
Neutral spray glaze: 300 g Absolu cristal
instructions: Morello cherry sorbet: heat the water; at 30C add sugar (reserving a little) and glucose, at 45C add stabilizer premixed with reserved sugar; cook to 85C and blend.
Cool to 4C, mature 12 hours, add the defrosted cherries, blend, churn and hold at -18C.
Basque shortbread: sand the dry ingredients with the butter, add the yolks and mix briefly; spread into two 18cm rings, eggwash with milk and bake 15-20 minutes at 160C.
Almond parfait: poach the whites and sugar in a bain-marie to 50C while whisking, then whip until cool.
Blend the cream, scraped vanilla, almond paste and mascarpone and whip to a chantilly, then gently fold the two masses together and use immediately.
Neutral glaze: bring all ingredients to a boil, cool to 60C and use immediately.
Smooth 175 g cherry sorbet per 14cm ring and mold the rest as quenelles; freeze.
On each shortbread pipe a thin spiral of parfait, set the sorbet insert on top, pipe parfait all around to cover completely, add cherries and sorbet quenelles and freeze.
Spray with the neutral glaze and decorate with chopped dragées.

title: Sandwich Glacé (Ice Cream Sandwich)
description: Layered frozen sandwich of pistachio-raspberry Joconde sponge with mango and raspberry sorbets, cut into triangles.
ingredients: Joconde sponge: 50 g pastry wheat flour T65
Joconde sponge: 50 g frozen raspberry chunks
instructions: Raspberry sorbet: heat the water; at 30C add sugar (reserving a little) and glucose, at 45C add stabilizer with reserved sugar; cook to 85C and blend.
Cool to 4C, mature 12 hours, add the melted raspberry purée, blend, churn and hold at -18C.
Mango sorbet: make the same way, adding the melted mango purée before churning and holding at -18C.
Joconde sponge: whip the egg whites with the sugar; separately whip the eggs, sifted icing sugar and almond powder to ribbon stage.
Fold the sifted flour into the whipped eggs, fold in the meringue, then incorporate the melted butter loosened with a little batter.
Spread on a silicone mat, sprinkle with raspberry chunks and chopped pistachios, bake 8 minutes at 170C and cut two 27x18cm rectangles.
In a 27x18x0.5cm frame place one sponge (pistachios down), add a frame and smooth mango sorbet, freeze; add a frame and smooth raspberry sorbet.
Top with the second sponge (pistachios up), freeze, then cut into 9cm squares and each square into 2 right triangles.

title: Bromélia
description: A tropical layered entremets pairing caramel bavaroise and pineapple with an almond-coconut dacquoise and a lime crunch base.
ingredients: Crumble: 70 g pastry wheat flour T65, 35 g caster sugar, 35 g brown sugar, 70 g almond powder, 1 g salt, 70 g butter. Crunch: 240 g baked crumble, 26 g butter, 26 g cocoa butter, 30 g brown sugar, zest of 1 lime. Almond coconut dacquoise: 54 g egg whites, 44 g caster sugar, 33 g almond powder, 10 g grated coconut, 26 g icing sugar, 13 g pastry wheat flour T65. Caramel pineapple cream: 1.2 g gelatin powder, 6 g water, 80 g caster sugar, 235 g pineapple purée, 1 g vanilla powder, 1 g salt, 33 g egg yolks, 12 g brown sugar, 15 g custard powder, 127 g butter. Caramel bavaroise: 9 g gelatin powder, 54 g water, 157 g semi-skimmed milk, 157 g cream 35%, 105 g caster sugar, 75 g egg yolks, 277 g cream 35%. Pineapple compote: zest of 0.5 lime, 295 g frozen diced pineapple, 20 g pineapple purée, 0.5 vanilla pod, 30 g caster sugar, 3 g NH pectin. Pineapple chips: 300 g pineapple, 100 g water, 100 g caster sugar. Dulcey spray: 50 g cocoa butter, 80 g Dulcey chocolate. Finishing: 50 g cold-use neutral glaze.
instructions: Crumble: sand all ingredients with the butter until homogeneous, sift, and bake 15 to 20 minutes at 160C. Crunch: mix butter and cocoa butter melted at 40C with brown sugar, lime zest and baked crumble; spread into two 14cm rings and freeze. Dacquoise: whip egg whites with the sugar, fold in the sifted powders, pipe a 16cm spiral per entremets, dust with icing sugar and bake about 10 minutes at 180C, then cut to 14cm. Caramel pineapple cream: boil the pineapple purée with vanilla and salt, dry-caramelize the sugar and deglaze with the hot pulp, cook with the yolks, brown sugar and custard powder like a pastry cream, off heat add rehydrated gelatin, cool to 40C, blend in the diced butter, spread over the dacquoise and freeze. Caramel bavaroise: boil milk and cream, dry-caramelize the sugar and deglaze, cook with blanched yolks and sugar to 84C, add rehydrated gelatin, cool to 20C and fold in the whipped cream. Pineapple compote: heat diced pineapple, purée, lime zest and scraped vanilla to 40C, add sugar mixed with pectin, boil and stew about 10 minutes, then pour into two 14cm rings and freeze. Chips: make a syrup with sugar and water, dip pineapple slices 1 minute, and dry several hours at 65C. Assembly: fill a 16cm ring halfway with bavaroise, add the cream/dacquoise insert, more bavaroise, then the crunch disc; freeze, spray with the melted Dulcey mixture, glaze the pineapple compote disc and set it on top, and decorate with pineapple chips.

title: Carburer Au Café
description: A dark chocolate and coffee entremets with a milk chocolate coffee cremeux, chocolate sponge and cocoa crumble under a shiny dark glaze.
ingredients: Cocoa crumble: 40 g pastry wheat flour T65, 10 g cocoa powder, 50 g caster sugar, 50 g almond powder, 2 g salt, 50 g butter. Chocolate sponge: 80 g Guanaja 70%, 80 g butter, 60 g egg yolks, 12 g pastry wheat flour T65, 12 g potato starch, 60 g egg whites, 24 g caster sugar. Milk coffee cremeux: 300 g Jivara milk 40%, 150 g semi-skimmed milk, 150 g cream 35%, 20 g coffee beans, 3 g soluble coffee, 60 g egg yolks, 30 g caster sugar. Dark chocolate bavaroise: 4 g gelatin powder, 24 g water, 95 g Guanaja 70%, 110 g semi-skimmed milk, 110 g cream 35%, 43 g egg yolks, 21 g caster sugar, 300 g cream 35%. Dark glaze: 15 g gelatin powder, 75 g water, 100 g water, 260 g caster sugar, 130 g cream 35%, 96 g glucose syrup DE38, 25 g invert sugar, 72 g cocoa powder. Finishing: 300 g Extra Bitter Guayakil 64%, 5 g coffee beans.
instructions: Cocoa crumble: sand all ingredients with the butter, roll to 2.5mm, cut a 14cm disc per entremets and bake 15 to 20 minutes at 160C. Chocolate sponge: whisk yolks with the chocolate and butter melted at 45C, fold in whites whipped with the sugar, then the sifted flour and starch, pipe a 14cm spiral per entremets and bake 10 minutes at 180C. Milk coffee cremeux: infuse the milk, cream and coffee beans 15 minutes, strain and re-weigh, bring back to a simmer, cook with blanched yolks, sugar and soluble coffee to 84C, emulsify onto the milk chocolate, pour over the sponge and freeze. Dark chocolate bavaroise: simmer milk and cream, cook with blanched yolks and sugar to 84C, add rehydrated gelatin, emulsify onto the chopped chocolate, cool to 20C and fold in the whipped cream. Dark glaze: cook water and sugar to 110C, boil the cream with glucose and invert sugar, add sifted cocoa and re-boil, combine with the cooked sugar, add rehydrated gelatin and cool. Assembly: fill a 16cm ring halfway with bavaroise, add the cremeux/sponge insert, more bavaroise, then the crumble disc; freeze, glaze at 26 to 28C and decorate with tempered dark chocolate and coffee beans.

title: Chocolat Orange & Caramel
description: Chocolate joconde fingers layered with orange marmalade and whipped Caramélia ganache, finished with cocoa nib tuile and candied orange zest.
ingredients: Joconde sponge: 35 g butter, 100 g almond powder, 100 g icing sugar, 215 g whole eggs, 125 g egg whites, 25 g caster sugar, 35 g pastry wheat flour T65, 15 g cocoa powder. Orange marmalade: 360 g orange purée, 52 g orange concentrate, 34 g caster sugar, 6 g agar agar, 190 g candied orange peel strips. Caramélia whipped ganache: 400 g Caramélia 36%, 910 g cream 35%, 25 g invert sugar, 25 g glucose syrup DE38. Cocoa nib tuile: 75 g caster sugar, 38 g cocoa nibs, 30 g orange purée, 19 g pastry wheat flour T65, 30 g butter. Orange zest: 1 orange, 300 g caster sugar, 200 g water, 1 g orange food coloring.
instructions: Joconde sponge: whip whole eggs with sifted icing sugar and almond powder to the ribbon, fold in the sifted flour and cocoa, then egg whites whipped with the caster sugar, and finish with the melted butter; spread on a mat, bake 8 minutes at 170C and cut six 16x16cm squares. Orange marmalade: heat the purée and concentrate to 40C, add sugar mixed with agar agar, boil while whisking, cool, blend, then fold in the brunoise candied orange. Caramélia ganache: simmer a third of the cream with invert sugar and glucose, emulsify onto the chopped chocolate, add remaining cream, blend and rest 12 hours refrigerated. Cocoa nib tuile: mix all ingredients with the melted butter, rest 12 hours, spread on a mat, bake 10 minutes at 180C and break into pieces. Orange zest: peel and blanch the zest 3 to 6 times from cold water, then confit in a syrup of water, sugar and coloring. Assembly: in a 16x16cm frame smooth marmalade over a joconde square, cover with a second sponge, whip and spread 200 g ganache, top with the last sponge and freeze; trim and cut into 2.5x12.5cm fingers, pipe whipped ganache on each, and decorate with tuile shards and candied orange zest.

title: Pomme & Nuts
description: A gianduja mousse entremets with a Calvados green apple compote, praline crunch and hazelnut sponge.
ingredients: Hazelnut sponge: 20 g butter, 20 g hazelnut paste, 20 g invert sugar, 34 g caster sugar, 20 g almond powder, 34 g pastry wheat flour T65, 2 g baking powder, 34 g cream 35%, 68 g whole eggs. Praline crunch: 20 g Jivara 40%, 130 g 50% almond/hazelnut praliné, 60 g feuilletine. Green apple compote: 5 Granny Smith apples, 15 g water, 35 g Calvados, 50 g caster sugar, 6 g NH pectin, 1 vanilla pod. Gianduja mousse: 4 g gelatin powder, 24 g water, 150 g semi-skimmed milk, 230 g milk gianduja, 300 g cream 35%. Spray mixture: 100 g cocoa butter, 160 g Jivara 40%. Finishing: 50 g cold-use neutral glaze, 50 g 50% almond/hazelnut praliné, 50 g skinned hazelnuts, 1 Granny Smith apple.
instructions: Hazelnut sponge: briefly mix the cream with the sifted dry ingredients, add the eggs, then the butter, hazelnut paste and invert sugar melted at 40C; pour into two 14cm rings and bake 5 to 6 minutes at 170C. Praline crunch: mix the chocolate melted at 45C with the praliné and feuilletine, spread over the sponge and freeze. Green apple compote: simmer the brunoise apples with water and scraped vanilla until translucent, cool to 40C, add sugar mixed with pectin, boil about 1 minute, add the Calvados, spread into two 14cm rings and freeze. Gianduja mousse: simmer the milk, add rehydrated gelatin, emulsify onto the gianduja, cool to 29C and fold in the whipped cream. Assembly: fill a 16cm ring halfway with mousse, add the apple compote and more mousse, place the crunch/sponge insert and smooth; freeze, spray with the melted cocoa butter and Jivara mixture at 35C, and decorate with lines of glaze mixed with praliné, green apple slices and roasted hazelnuts.

title: Tête De Linotte
description: A milk chocolate mousse entremets over a caramel cream, pecan brownie and sweet pastry base, finished with a milk chocolate glaze.
ingredients: Sweet pastry: 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 60 g butter, 40 g icing sugar, 1 g salt, 8 g almond powder, 20 g whole eggs. Brownie: 52 g butter, 1 g salt, 95 g caster sugar, 47 g whole eggs, 13 g Guanaja 70%, 26 g 100% cocoa paste, 38 g pastry wheat flour T65, 50 g pecan nuts. Caramel cream: 4 g gelatin powder, 24 g water, 240 g cream 35%, 60 g glucose syrup DE38, 120 g caster sugar, 72 g salted butter. Milk chocolate mousse: 3 g gelatin powder, 18 g water, 215 g Jivara 40%, 155 g semi-skimmed milk, 310 g cream 35%. Milk chocolate glaze: 15 g gelatin powder, 75 g water, 225 g Jivara 40%, 112 g water, 225 g glucose syrup DE38, 225 g caster sugar, 150 g unsweetened condensed milk. Finishing: 300 g Jivara 40%.
instructions: Sweet pastry: sand the dry ingredients with the butter, add the eggs and knead briefly, chill, roll to 2.5mm, cut a 14cm disc per entremets plus 3cm squares for decor, bake 15 minutes at 155C, then eggwash and bake another 5 to 10 minutes. Brownie: lightly whisk the eggs, sugar and salt, add the sifted flour, then the chocolate, cocoa paste and butter melted at 45C, fold in the crushed pecans, spread over the baked pastry and bake 10 to 15 minutes at 170C. Caramel cream: boil the cream, dry-caramelize the sugar and glucose and deglaze with the hot cream, recook to 103C, add rehydrated gelatin, cool to 40C, blend in the diced butter, pour over the brownie and freeze. Milk chocolate mousse: simmer the milk, add rehydrated gelatin, emulsify onto the chocolate, cool to 25C and fold in the whipped cream. Milk chocolate glaze: boil water and sugar with the glucose to 103C, add the condensed milk and re-boil, add rehydrated gelatin, emulsify onto the chocolate and cool to 30C. Assembly: fill a 16cm ring halfway with mousse, add the caramel cream/brownie/pastry insert and smooth; freeze, glaze at 30C, and decorate with tempered milk chocolate and pastry squares.

title: Fougasse aux Olives
description: A Provençal flatbread studded with black and green olives and Herbs of Provence.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the water at base temperature (54-58 C), then add the flours, fermented dough, Herbs of Provence and salt.
Knead with the hook 3 minutes on 1st speed, then 6 minutes on 2nd speed.
Add the bassinage water in a thin stream at the end of 2nd speed.
Add the drained, quartered olives on 1st speed; final dough temperature 24 C.
First proof 1 hour at room temperature.
Divide into 370 g pieces, roll lightly into ovals and rest 15 minutes, then shape.
Second proof about 1 hour at 24 C.
Bake in a deck oven 10 to 12 minutes at 250 C.

title: Guimauve Passion au Sucre Inverti
description: A passion fruit marshmallow made with invert sugar, set in a frame and cut into sugared cubes (yield is one 20x20 cm frame; estimated at 36 cubes).
instructions: Make the acid solution: bring the water to a simmer, add the citric acid and stir until dissolved, then cover tightly.
Cook the passion fruit puree, caster sugar and the 80 g of invert sugar to 110 C.
Off the heat, stop the cooking with the rehydrated gelatin.
Pour over the 100 g of invert sugar and whip together; add the coloring.
Add the acid solution when the marshmallow is almost cooled.
Spread and smooth into a greased 20x20 cm frame and let set 12 hours at room temperature.
Cut into cubes and roll in a 50/50 mix of icing sugar and cornstarch.

title: Levain Dur Naturel aux Pommes
description: A natural stiff sourdough starter built from wild apple ferment and successive flour refreshes (yield about 1 kg; portioned here as roughly 20 x 50 g).
ingredients: 500 g fermentation base (apple juice), 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65 (first refresh)
500 g first refresh, 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65, 500 g water (second refresh)
250 g second refresh, 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65, 250 g water (third refresh)
250 g third refresh, 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65, 250 g water (ready-to-use sourdough)
instructions: Cut the apples into pieces, put in a tub with the water, cover with film and macerate 24 hours at 20-25 C, then strain to collect the apple juice.
First refresh: mix the apple juice with the flour, knead 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 24 hours at 25 C.
Second refresh: knead the ingredients 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 24 hours at 25 C.
Third refresh: knead 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 24 hours at 25 C.
Ready-to-use refresh: knead 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 4 hours at 20 C.
Store at 4 C.

title: Levain Liquide Naturel aux Pommes
description: A natural liquid sourdough starter built from wild apple ferment and successive flour-and-water refreshes (yield about 1 kg; portioned here as roughly 20 x 50 g).
ingredients: 500 g fermentation base (apple juice), 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65 (first refresh, mother starter)
500 g first starter, 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65, 500 g water (second refresh)
500 g second starter, 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65, 500 g water (third refresh)
250 g third starter, 500 g Tradition wheat flour T65, 500 g water (ready-to-use sourdough)
instructions: Cut the apples into pieces, put in a tub with the water, cover with film and macerate 24 hours at 20-25 C, then strain to collect the apple juice.
First refresh: mix the apple juice with the flour, knead 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 24 hours at 25 C.
Second refresh: knead the ingredients 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 24 hours at 25 C.
Third refresh: knead 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 24 hours at 25 C.
Ready-to-use refresh: knead 5 minutes on 1st speed, cover and ferment 4 hours at 20 C.
Store at 4 C.

title: Tarte Fraise Pistache Glacée (Frozen Strawberry & Pistachio Tarts)
description: Frozen finger tarts of pistachio ice cream over strawberry jam and pistachio Joconde on a buckwheat crumble, coated in crunchy white chocolate and topped with pistachio chantilly.
ingredients: Pistachio ice cream: 250 g whole milk
Pistachio ice cream: 50 g liquid cream 35%
Pistachio ice cream: 12 g invert sugar
Pistachio ice cream: 50 g caster sugar
Pistachio ice cream: 62 g egg yolks
Pistachio ice cream: 35 g pistachio paste
Pistachio ice cream: 1 g glycerol monostearate
Buckwheat crumble: 50 g pastry wheat flour T65
Buckwheat crumble: 40 g whole hazelnut powder
Joconde sponge: 25 g pastry wheat flour T65
Crunchy coating: 500 g Ivoire 35% white chocolate
instructions: Pistachio ice cream: heat the milk; at 30C add invert sugar and caster sugar (reserving a little), at 35C add cream, at 40C add yolks and pistachio paste, at 45C add stabilizer, monostearate and reserved sugar.
Cook to 85C, blend, cool to 4C, mature 12 hours, blend again, churn and hold at -18C.
Buckwheat crumble: sand all ingredients with the butter to a homogeneous dough, roll to 3mm, cut 6 sole-size oblongs and screen the rest; bake 15-20 minutes at 160C.
Strawberry juice: seal the strawberries, sugar and lemon in a filmed bowl and heat in a water bath at least 1 hour, strain without crushing and keep the cooked berries for the jam.
Strawberry jelly: warm part of the juice, dissolve the rehydrated gelatin, add the rest, pour 1cm thick in a 16x16cm frame and freeze.

Joconde sponge: whip whites with sugar, whip eggs, icing sugar and almond powder to ribbon, fold in flour, then the whites, then the butter softened with pistachio paste; spread and bake 8 minutes at 170C, cut 6 insert oblongs.
Strawberry jam: heat the chopped strawberries and lemon to 40C, add the sugar premixed with NH pectin, boil 30 seconds whisking and cool quickly.
Crunchy coating: mix the chocolate melted at 45C with grapeseed oil, pistachio paste and roasted pistachios; use at 35C.
Pistachio chantilly: whip the cream, mascarpone, pistachio paste and sugar to a chantilly and use immediately.
Place a sponge in each finger mold, pipe about 1cm strawberry jam and set in the freezer, then fill flush with pistachio ice cream and smooth.

Glaze the frozen fingers with the crunchy coating, set on the crumble, pipe 3 drops of pistachio chantilly and decorate with glazed half-strawberries, roasted pistachios and cubes of strawberry jelly.

title: Vacherin Fraise Vanille (Strawberry & Vanilla Vacherin)
description: Individual vacherins of Swiss meringue shells filled with chantilly and vanilla ice cream, topped with raspberry-glazed strawberry sorbet and a glucose tuile.
ingredients: Vanilla ice cream: 400 g whole milk
Vanilla ice cream: 65 g powdered milk 0%
Vanilla ice cream: 160 g caster sugar
Vanilla ice cream: 60 g powdered glucose
Vanilla ice cream: 185 g liquid cream 35%
Vanilla ice cream: 75 g egg yolks
Vanilla ice cream: 3 g glycerol monostearate
Raspberry gel: 60 g glucose syrup DE38
Glucose tuile: 250 g glucose syrup DE38
instructions: Strawberry sorbet: heat the water; at 30C add sugar (reserving a little) and glucose, at 45C add stabilizer with reserved sugar; cook to 85C and blend.
Cool to 4C, mature 12 hours, add hulled strawberries, blend, churn and hold at -18C.

Vanilla ice cream: heat milk, scraped vanilla and milk powder; add sugar and glucose at 30C, cream at 35C, yolks at 40C, stabilizer and monostearate at 45C; cook to 85C, blend, mature 12 hours, churn and hold at -18C.
Swiss meringue: poach whites and sugar to 50C whisking, whip until cool, pipe spirals on greased 6cm half-spheres and pipe strips dusted with red sugar; bake at 90C for several hours.
Chantilly cream: whip the cream, mascarpone and sugar to a chantilly and use immediately.
Raspberry gel: heat all ingredients to 60C, blend and cool quickly.
Glucose tuile: heat the glucose with coloring, spread thinly between two silicone mats and bake 12-15 minutes at 150C.
Fill 5cm half-spheres with vanilla ice cream and 6cm half-spheres with strawberry sorbet; freeze, then glaze the sorbet spheres with raspberry gel at 30C.
Waterproof the meringue shells with melted cocoa butter and white chocolate, fill with chantilly, insert a vanilla ice cream half-sphere and smooth flush with chantilly.
Set a glazed strawberry sorbet half-sphere on each, pipe a chantilly collar at its base and finish with a half strawberry, meringue chunks and a glucose tuile.

title: Flan
description: A classic French custard tart with a starch-set vanilla cream baked in a crisp pie pastry shell.
ingredients: Pie pastry: 105 g pastry wheat flour T65, 30 g potato starch, 76 g butter, 2 g salt, 3 g caster sugar, 10 g egg yolks, 28 g semi-skimmed milk. Flan custard: 450 g semi-skimmed milk, 150 g cream (35%), 1 vanilla pod, 90 g whole eggs, 36 g egg yolks, 150 g caster sugar, 48 g cornstarch. Finishing: 10 g water, 100 g decoration sugar, 5 g neutral hot glaze.
instructions: Sand all the dry pastry ingredients with the butter. Add the liquid ingredients and knead the dough briefly, then cool quickly. Roll out to 2.5 mm and line two 16 cm entremets rings; set aside in the fridge. For the custard, warm the milk, cream and scraped vanilla pods. Blanch the eggs, yolks and sugar, then add the cornstarch and mix. Add part of the hot milk and cream mixture and mix well, then cook everything until the starch slackens. Immediately pour into the cold lined rings and spread. Bake about 45 minutes at 170 C. Once cold, glaze the flans and sprinkle their edges with decoration sugar.

title: Tarte Aux Pommes
description: A sweet pastry tart layered with spiced apple compote and topped with a rosette of thinly sliced glazed apples.
ingredients: Sweet pastry: 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 60 g butter, 40 g icing sugar, 8 g almond powder, 20 g whole eggs, 1 g salt. Apple compote: 3 Golden apples, caster sugar (10% of apple weight), vanilla powder, cinnamon powder. Apple filling: 4 Golden apples, 50 g caster sugar, 50 g butter. Assembly and finishing: 10 g water, 100 g neutral hot glaze, 5 g decoration sugar.
instructions: Sand the dry pastry ingredients with the butter, add the eggs and knead briefly, then cool quickly. Roll out to 2.5 mm, line two 18 cm tart rings, prick, and refrigerate. For the compote, dice the apples into brunoise and cook covered with the sugar, vanilla and cinnamon; once translucent, continue uncovered to dry the compote, then cool quickly. For the filling, finely slice the apples to 1 mm and use immediately. Spread the compote in the lined shells, arrange the apple slices in an overlapping rosette, brush with butter and sprinkle with sugar. Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 155 C. Once cold, glaze and sprinkle the edges with decoration sugar.

title: Raspberry Molded Caramel Bonbons
description: Molded dark chocolate shells with a red-sprayed decor, filled with a soft raspberry caramel and sealed.
instructions: Melt cocoa butter at 45C, color red, temper to 28-30C and spray the mold in the desired pattern.
Melt and temper the dark chocolate, line the mold and crystallize at 17C.
Cook the cream, sugar and glucose to 120C while whisking, deglaze with raspberry puree and invert sugar, then recook to 106C.
Add the butter off the heat and blend, cool to 29C and fill the shells 3/4 full.
Crystallize 24 hours at 17C, then seal with tempered dark chocolate, set 1 hour at 17C and unmold.

title: Tarte Bourdaloue
description: A sweet pastry tart filled with almond cream and poached pear halves, finished with roasted sliced almonds.
ingredients: Sweet pastry: 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 60 g butter, 40 g icing sugar, 10 g almond powder, 20 g whole eggs, 1 g salt. Almond cream: 40 g butter, 40 g caster sugar, 40 g whole eggs, 40 g almond powder. Poached pears: 500 g water, 250 g caster sugar, 1 g ascorbic acid, 3 pears. Assembly and finishing: 200 g neutral hot glaze, 50 g sliced almonds, 10 g decoration sugar.
instructions: Sand the dry pastry ingredients with the butter, add the eggs and knead briefly, then cool quickly. Roll out to 2.5 mm, line one 18 cm tart ring, prick, and refrigerate. For the almond cream, mix the soft butter, sugar and almond powder until homogeneous, then add the eggs a little at a time without overmixing; spread in the cold lined shell and cool. Bring the water and sugar to a boil, add the ascorbic acid, then poach the peeled, cored, halved pears in the simmering syrup and let cool in the syrup. Drain and slice the pear halves, placing 5 halves per tart on the almond cream. Bake about 30 minutes at 160 C. Once cold, glaze and decorate with roasted sliced almonds and decoration sugar.

title: Fraisier
description: The classic French strawberry entremet layering génoise sponge, vanilla diplomat cream and fresh strawberries, finished with a chantilly crown and glazed strawberries.
ingredients: Génoise sponge: 240 g whole eggs, 120 g caster sugar, 120 g pastry wheat flour T65, 10 g butter and 10 g pastry wheat flour T65 (for the rings)
Vanilla diplomat cream: 300 g semi-skimmed milk, 1 vanilla pod, 100 g egg yolks, 110 g caster sugar, 24 g custard powder, 6 g gelatin powder, 36 g water, 300 g cream (35%)
Soaking syrup: 160 g water, 216 g caster sugar, 10 g strawberry liquor
Assembly and finishing: 1000 g strawberries, 100 g neutral cold glaze, 200 g cream (35%), 20 g caster sugar, 10 g pistachios
instructions: Génoise: poach the eggs and sugar in a bain-marie to 45C, whip to a cold ribbon, fold in the sifted flour, divide into two buttered and floured 16cm rings, and bake 25 minutes at 160C.

Vanilla diplomat cream: warm the milk with scraped vanilla; blanch yolks and sugar, add custard powder, temper with hot milk, cook until the starch slackens, off heat add rehydrated gelatin. Cool, smooth with a whisk, then fold in the softly whipped cream in three additions; use immediately.
Soaking syrup: make a syrup with water and sugar, cool, then add the strawberry liquor.

Assembly: cut each génoise into three 14cm disks 1cm thick, line a 16cm ring with halved strawberries, place a soaked disk in the base, pipe a spiral of diplomat cream, add strawberry brunoise, cover with more cream, add a second soaked disk and smooth level with diplomat cream, then set in the fridge.
Finishing: whip the cream with sugar to chantilly, pipe a ring of drops around the edge with a Saint Honoré tip, cover the surface with glazed strawberries, and scatter chopped pistachios.

title: Tarte Citron Meringuee
description: A blind-baked sweet pastry shell filled with tangy lemon cream and topped with torched Italian meringue.
ingredients: Sweet pastry: 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 60 g butter, 40 g icing sugar, 10 g almond powder, 20 g whole eggs, 1 g salt. Lemon cream: 90 g lemon puree, 150 g whole eggs, 120 g caster sugar, 2 g gelatin powder, 12 g water, 75 g butter. Italian meringue: 80 g water, 240 g caster sugar, 120 g egg whites. Finishing: 10 g icing sugar.
instructions: Sand the dry pastry ingredients with the butter, add the eggs and knead briefly, then cool quickly. Roll out to 2.5 mm, line two 18 cm tart rings and prick. Blind bake 20 minutes at 155 C, egg wash and finish baking 5 to 10 minutes. For the lemon cream, bring the lemon juice to a boil, blanch the eggs and sugar, add part of the hot juice, then boil while whisking; off the heat add the rehydrated gelatin, cool to 40 C, add the diced butter and blend. Pour into the baked shells and freeze. For the meringue, cook a water and sugar syrup to 118 C, whip the egg whites until soft, pour in the syrup and whip until cold. Pipe over the lemon cream to cover completely, dust with icing sugar and caramelize lightly with a blowtorch or 2 minutes at 230 C.

title: Tarte Tatin
description: The classic upside-down caramelized apple tart baked under a disk of pie pastry and glazed after unmolding.
ingredients: Pie pastry: 105 g pastry wheat flour T65, 30 g potato starch, 76 g butter, 2 g salt, 3 g caster sugar, 10 g egg yolks, 28 g semi-skimmed milk. Caramel: 75 g caster sugar, 35 g butter. Apple filling: 6 Golden apples (about 900 g). Finishing: 200 g neutral hot glaze.
instructions: Sand the dry pastry ingredients with the butter, add the liquid ingredients and knead briefly, then cool quickly. Roll out to 2.5 mm and cut one 22 cm disk; refrigerate. Dry caramelize the sugar and stop the cooking with the butter, then pour immediately into a cake tin lined with parchment. Peel the apples, cut them in half vertically and seed them, then arrange the halves over the caramel. Bake 35 minutes at 170 C, remove, flatten the apples and let cool. Lay the pastry disk over the apples and bake 25 minutes at 170 C, then freeze. Unmold the frozen tart using a blowtorch and glaze with hot glaze.

title: Chouquettes
description: Classic small choux puffs baked until crisp and topped with crunchy pearl sugar.
instructions: Bring the water, butter, sugar and salt to a boil.
Off the heat, add the sifted flour and mix well.
Dry the panade over the heat, then let it cool while mixing with the paddle.
Add the eggs gradually until the dough is smooth and shiny.
On a greased baking sheet, pipe 3 cm choux with a 10 mm round tip.
Sprinkle the chouquettes with pearl sugar.
Bake in a fan oven at 140 C for 25 minutes, then at 160 C for 15 minutes.

title: Exotic Coconut Bonbons
description: Framed dark chocolate bonbons layering coconut praline with a passionfruit milk-chocolate ganache, cut into rectangles and enrobed.
instructions: Heat the 15 g passion fruit puree and sugar until dissolved, add grated coconut, roast 10-12 minutes at 150C, cool and lightly blend to make caramelized coconut.
Melt 50 g dark chocolate at 35-40C, pre-coat a sheet of baking paper and stick a 5mm ganache frame; let set.
Melt the Jivara and cocoa butter at 40C, add the praline and caramelized coconut, temper to 24C and smooth into the frame.
Stick the 17.5x17.5x0.8cm frame and let crystallize.
Bring the 60 g passion puree, invert sugar and butter to a simmer, pour over melted milk chocolate and emulsify, then smooth over the coconut praline.
Crystallize 24 hours at 17C, then cut into 1.5x4cm bonbons.
Melt and temper 150 g dark chocolate, dip each bonbon and decorate with grated coconut.

title: Choux Pistache Framboise
description: Craquelin-topped double choux filled with raspberry compote and whipped pistachio cream, finished with a raspberry glaze disc.
ingredients: Craquelin: 50 g butter, 60 g brown sugar, 60 g pastry wheat flour T65
Choux pastry: 80 g butter, 200 g water, 4 g caster sugar, 4 g salt, 120 g pastry wheat flour T65, 200 g whole eggs
Raspberry compote: 14 g caster sugar, 2.5 g NH pectin, 120 g raspberry puree, 8 g invert sugar, 16 g glucose syrup DE38
Pistachio cream: 5.5 g gelatin powder, 33 g water, 270 g 35% cream, 41 g egg yolks, 54 g caster sugar, 32 g pistachio paste, 135 g 35% cream, 135 g mascarpone
Raspberry glaze: 150 g raspberry puree, 15 g caster sugar, 3 g NH pectin
Finishing: 50 g chopped pistachios, 50 g cold neutral glaze, 50 g raspberries, 20 g decoration sugar, 50 g pistachios
instructions: Craquelin: sand all ingredients into a smooth paste, roll to 1-2 mm between two papers, freeze.
Choux: boil water, butter, sugar and salt; off heat add sifted flour; dry the panade; cool; add eggs gradually to a smooth shiny dough.
Pipe ten 5 cm choux (14 mm tip) and ten 3 cm choux (10 mm tip); top each with a matching craquelin disc.
Bake at 140 C for 25 minutes, then 160 C for 10-15 minutes.
Raspberry compote: heat puree, invert sugar and glucose to 40 C, add premixed sugar and pectin, boil 1 minute whisking, cool.
Pistachio cream: heat 270 g cream; blanch yolks and sugar, temper with cream, cook to 84 C; add gelatin, pistachio paste, remaining cream and mascarpone, blend; chill 12 hours.
Raspberry glaze: heat puree to 40 C, add premixed sugar and pectin, boil 1 minute, spread 1.5-2 mm and freeze.
Fill small choux with compote; halve large choux and coat base edges with chopped pistachios set with glaze.
Whip pistachio cream, fill large choux, seat a small choux, pipe a rosette to cover it.
Close, top with a 4 cm raspberry glaze disc, and decorate with a sugared raspberry and pistachios.

title: Éclairs Crousti-Fondant Vanille
description: Craquelin-topped éclairs filled with vanilla pastry cream and a crunchy praline-cereal crisp, piped with whipped vanilla cream.
ingredients: Craquelin: 50 g butter, 60 g brown sugar, 60 g pastry wheat flour T65
Choux pastry: 80 g butter, 200 g water, 4 g caster sugar, 4 g salt, 120 g pastry wheat flour T65, 200 g whole eggs
Vanilla pastry cream: 500 g semi-skimmed milk, 100 g caster sugar, 60 g egg yolks, 25 g custard powder, 25 g pastry wheat flour T65, 0.5 vanilla pod
Vanilla cream: 3.3 g gelatin powder, 17 g water, 210 g 35% cream, 0.5 vanilla pod, 41 g egg yolks, 47 g caster sugar, 105 g mascarpone, 105 g 35% cream
Crunch: 15 g corn flakes, 10 g puffed rice, 10 g pine nuts, 60 g Ivoire 35% white chocolate, 1 g vanilla powder
instructions: Craquelin: sand all ingredients, roll to 1-2 mm between two papers, freeze.
Choux: boil water, butter, sugar and salt; off heat add sifted flour; dry the panade; cool; add eggs gradually to a smooth shiny dough.
Pipe 12 cm éclairs with a 14 mm tip; top each with a 2.5x12 cm craquelin rectangle.
Bake at 140 C for 25 minutes, then 160 C for 15 minutes.
Vanilla pastry cream: warm milk and vanilla; blanch yolks and sugar, add custard powder and flour, temper with hot milk, cook until the starch slackens, cool quickly.
Vanilla cream: heat 210 g cream with vanilla; blanch yolks and sugar, temper, cook to 84 C; add gelatin, then remaining cream and mascarpone, blend; chill 12 hours.
Crunch: gently fold cereals, pine nuts and vanilla into white chocolate melted at 40 C; drop small nuggets on paper and set.
Cut éclairs horizontally at two-thirds height; fill with pastry cream and crunch nuggets.
Whip the vanilla cream and pipe a zig-zag with a Saint Honoré tip; decorate with crunch nuggets.

title: Paris-Brest
description: Almond-hazelnut crusted choux ring filled with praline mousseline cream and dusted with snow sugar.
ingredients: Choux pastry: 80 g butter, 200 g water, 4 g caster sugar, 4 g salt, 120 g pastry wheat flour T65, 200 g whole eggs
Baking: 50 g whole almonds, 50 g whole hazelnuts
Praline mousseline cream: 270 g semi-skimmed milk, 60 g egg yolks, 80 g caster sugar, 21 g custard powder, 215 g butter, 130 g 50% almond/hazelnut praline, 33 g hazelnut paste
Finishing: 50 g 50% almond/hazelnut praline, 10 g decoration sugar
instructions: Choux: boil water, butter, sugar and salt; off heat add sifted flour; dry the panade; cool; add eggs gradually to a smooth shiny dough.
For the large cake, pipe a 16 cm triple choux ring (14 mm tip) plus a separate 16 cm ring; for individuals pipe eight 8 cm rings.
Sprinkle rings with chopped almonds and hazelnuts (except the plain insert ring) and bake at 140 C for 25 minutes, then 160 C for 15-20 minutes.
Praline mousseline: cook milk, yolks, sugar and custard powder like a pastry cream; cool, smooth and temper.
Whip butter with praline and hazelnut paste until light, then blend in the smoothed pastry cream in two additions; use immediately.
Halve the rings, pipe praline on the base, then pipe the mousseline cream (tears for the large cake, spiral for individuals).
Close and dust with snow sugar.

title: Religieuses Citron
description: Stacked lemon choux with lemon cream insert, whipped lemon ganache, glazed almond paste and a cold meringue drop.
ingredients: Craquelin: 50 g butter, 60 g brown sugar, 60 g pastry wheat flour T65
Choux pastry: 80 g butter, 200 g water, 4 g caster sugar, 4 g salt, 120 g pastry wheat flour T65, 200 g whole eggs
Shortbread: 200 g pastry wheat flour T65, 120 g butter, 80 g icing sugar, 16 g almond powder, 40 g whole eggs, 2 g salt
Lemon cream: 63 g butter, 2 g gelatin powder, 12 g water, 75 g lemon puree, 125 g whole eggs, 100 g caster sugar
Lemon whipped ganache: 3 g gelatin powder, 15 g water, 68 g Ivoire 35% white chocolate, 250 g 35% cream, 0.5 lemon zest, 113 g lemon puree
Cold meringue: 60 g egg whites, 60 g caster sugar, 24 g glucose syrup DE38, 36 g invert sugar
Finishing: 175 g 50% almond paste, 0.5 g yellow food coloring, 50 g cold neutral glaze
instructions: Craquelin: sand all ingredients, roll to 1-2 mm, freeze.
Choux: boil water, butter, sugar and salt; off heat add sifted flour; dry the panade; cool; add eggs gradually to a smooth shiny dough.
Pipe ten 5 cm choux (14 mm tip) and ten 2.5 cm choux (10 mm tip); top each with a matching craquelin disc; bake at 140 C for 25 minutes, then 160 C for 10-15 minutes.
Shortbread: sand dry ingredients with butter, add eggs, knead briefly, chill, roll to 2 mm, cut discs, bake 15 minutes at 155 C between two Silpain.
Lemon cream: boil lemon puree, eggs and sugar while whisking; off heat add gelatin; cool to 40 C, add butter, blend; pipe into 3 cm hemispheres and freeze.
Lemon ganache: simmer a third of the cream, add gelatin, pour over white chocolate and lemon zest, emulsify, add remaining cream and lemon puree, blend, rest 12 hours at 4 C.
Cold meringue: warm whites with the sugars to 45 C over a bain-marie, whip to a firm cool meringue, use immediately.
Fill small choux with whipped lemon ganache; fill large choux with ganache, insert a lemon cream hemisphere, top up and close.
Color the almond paste, roll thin, cut ten 5 cm discs, glaze and stick onto the large choux.
Stack small choux on large ones; decorate with a large drop of cold meringue and shortbread discs.

title: Saint-Honoré
description: Puff pastry base ringed with choux and caramelized choux puffs, filled with Chiboust cream and piped with vanilla Chantilly.
ingredients: Rough puff pastry: 250 g pastry wheat flour T65, 5 g salt, 125 g water, 200 g dry butter
Choux pastry: 80 g butter, 200 g water, 4 g caster sugar, 4 g salt, 120 g pastry wheat flour T65, 200 g whole eggs

Chiboust cream: 3 g gelatin powder, 15 g water, 250 g semi-skimmed milk, 50 g egg yolks, 38 g caster sugar, 25 g custard powder, vanilla powder to taste, 35 g water, 100 g caster sugar, 90 g egg whites
Chantilly cream: 400 g 35% cream, 40 g caster sugar, 1 g vanilla powder
Assembly caramel: 65 g water, 200 g caster sugar, 20 g glucose syrup DE38
instructions: Rough puff: dissolve salt in water, add flour and cold dry butter, knead briefly without developing gluten, roll rectangular, rest; give 5 single folds resting 10 minutes between each; roll to 2 mm, prick, cut two 20 cm discs, chill.
Choux: boil water, butter, sugar and salt; off heat add sifted flour; dry the panade; cool; add eggs gradually to a smooth shiny dough.
Pipe a choux ring on the outer edge of each puff disc plus a fine inner spiral; pipe 2.5 cm choux separately (10 mm tip).
Bake at 140 C for 25 minutes, then 160 C for 15-20 minutes.
Chiboust: cook milk, vanilla, yolks, sugar and custard powder like a pastry cream, add gelatin; cook a 118 C syrup and whip into the whites; fold both together at 35 C; use immediately.
Chantilly: whip cream with vanilla sugar to a firm texture.
Fill small choux with Chiboust; pipe a Chiboust spiral inside the Saint-Honoré.
Cook a blond caramel with water, sugar and glucose, stop it in cold water, glaze the choux and fix them onto the choux ring.
Pipe Chantilly over the Chiboust with a Saint-Honoré tip.

title: Charlotte aux Framboises
description: A classic raspberry charlotte with a ladyfinger sponge shell, vanilla Bavarian mousse, a frozen raspberry crémeux insert, and a whipped vanilla ganache crown topped with fresh raspberries.
ingredients: Ladyfinger sponge: 180 g egg whites, 180 g caster sugar, 120 g egg yolks, 180 g pastry wheat flour T65, 60 g icing sugar (for baking)
Raspberry cream: 160 g raspberry purée, 64 g egg yolks, 48 g whole eggs, 40 g caster sugar, 3 g gelatin powder, 15 g water, 60 g butter
Vanilla Bavarian mousse: 320 g semi-skimmed milk, 1 vanilla pod, 80 g egg yolks, 128 g caster sugar, 9.5 g gelatin powder, 57 g water, 320 g cream (35%)
Syrup: 160 g water, 216 g caster sugar, 10 g raspberry flavor
Vanilla whipped ganache: 75 g white chocolate (Ivoire 35%), 3 g gelatin powder, 15 g water, 350 g cream (35%), 0.5 vanilla pod
Assembly and finishing: 250 g raspberries, 10 g decoration (snow) sugar
instructions: Ladyfinger sponge: whip the egg whites, adding the sugar progressively, then fold in the yolks gently followed by the sifted flour.

Using a 10mm round tip, pipe two 16cm disks and one 6.5x60cm cartridge belt per charlotte, sprinkle twice with icing sugar, and bake about 10 minutes at 180C. Trim disks to 14cm and the belt to 6cm tall.

Raspberry cream: bring the raspberry purée to a simmer; blanch yolks, whole eggs and sugar, add some hot purée, then boil while whisking. Off heat add rehydrated gelatin, cool to 40C, blend in diced butter, pour into two 14cm rings and freeze.

Vanilla Bavarian mousse: warm the milk with scraped vanilla; blanch yolks and sugar, temper with hot milk, cook everything to 84C, off heat add rehydrated gelatin. Cool to 17C and fold in the softly whipped cream; use immediately.
Syrup: make a syrup with water and sugar, cool, then add the raspberry liquor.

Vanilla whipped ganache: simmer a third of the cream with the vanilla, off heat add rehydrated gelatin, pour over the chopped white chocolate to emulsify, add the remaining cream, blend and refrigerate at least 12 hours.

Assembly: line a 16cm ring with the sponge cartridge, place a soaked disk in the base, pour bavarian mousse, add the raspberry crémeux insert then more mousse, cover with a second soaked disk, top up with mousse to 3mm below the rim and freeze.
Finishing: whip the vanilla ganache and pipe a ring around the edge with a Saint Honoré tip, fill the center with raspberries, and dust with snow sugar.

title: Dacquoise aux Fruits
