description: An almond dacquoise tart shell filled with orange mousseline cream and piled high with glazed seasonal fresh fruit.
ingredients: Dacquoise sponge: 67 g icing sugar, 113 g almond powder, 33 g pastry wheat flour T65, 133 g egg whites, 113 g caster sugar, zest of 1 orange, 12 g icing sugar (for dusting)
Orange mousseline cream: 288 g semi-skimmed milk, zest of 1 orange, 42 g egg yolks, 42 g caster sugar, 15 g custard powder, 15 g pastry wheat flour T65, 135 g butter
Finishing: 600 g seasonal fruits, 150 g neutral cold glaze
instructions: Dacquoise: whip the egg whites, gradually adding the caster sugar, then gently fold in the sifted mixed powders and orange zest.

Using a 14mm round tip, pipe a dacquoise spiral inside a greased and paper-lined 16cm ring, pipe a ring of dacquoise tears around the perimeter to form the tart edge, dust with icing sugar, and bake 20 to 25 minutes at 180C.
Orange mousseline cream: cook the milk, orange zest, yolks, sugar, custard powder and flour like a pastry cream, cool quickly, then smooth with a whisk and temper.
Beat the butter until light, then add the smooth pastry cream in two additions; use immediately.
Finishing: pipe a spiral of orange mousseline cream inside the dacquoise using a 10mm round tip, then cover it completely with cut and glazed fruit, building up volume.

title: Ispahan
description: Pierre Herme's signature rose-lychee-raspberry entremet built between two large macaron shells with rose petal buttercream, fresh raspberries and chopped lychees.
ingredients: Macaron shells: 225 g almond powder, 225 g icing sugar, 83 g egg whites, 221 g caster sugar, 56 g water, 83 g egg whites, 1 g powdered egg whites, 1 g red food coloring
Italian meringue: 47 g egg whites, 94 g caster sugar, 28 g water, 6 g caster sugar
Rose petal cream: 68 g semi-skimmed milk, 53 g egg yolks, 68 g caster sugar, 281 g butter, 131 g Italian meringue, 53 g butter, 3 g natural rose flavoring, 20 g rose syrup
Finishing: 300 g lychees, 450 g raspberries, 1 portion rose petals
instructions: Macaron shells: blend almond powder and icing sugar, mix in 83 g tempered egg whites and the coloring; cook water and caster sugar to 118C, whip the second 83 g of egg whites and pour in the syrup, whipping until warm.
Fold the warm meringue into the almond mixture and macaronner until glossy and ribboning; using a 12mm round tip, pipe 15cm macarons (2 per entremet) and bake about 22 minutes at 140C.
Italian meringue: cook water and sugar to 118C, whip the egg whites soft, pour in the syrup and whip until cool.

Rose petal cream: cook the milk, yolks and sugar to 85C, cool the anglaise to 30-35C, whip in the diced butter until smooth, stir in the Italian meringue, then add the second butter, rose syrup and flavoring and whip until light; use immediately.

Finishing: spray the shell interiors with water, pipe rose cream in a spiral on the base shell to 1cm from the edge, arrange raspberries in crowns with chopped lychees, pipe more rose cream, close with the second shell, and decorate with rose petals and raspberries.

title: Raspberry Framed Ganache Bonbons
description: Framed dark chocolate raspberry ganache spiked with raspberry liquor, cut into rectangles and hand-dipped.
instructions: Melt 50 g dark chocolate at 35-40C, pre-coat a sheet of baking paper and stick the ganache frame; let set.
Bring the raspberry puree, invert sugar, caster sugar and butter to a simmer.
Pour over the chopped 190 g dark chocolate, add the raspberry liquor and emulsify.
Smooth into the frame and crystallize 24 hours at 17C, then cut into 3x2.2cm rectangles.
Melt and temper 150 g dark chocolate, dip each bonbon and mark it with the fork.

title: Royal (Trianon)
description: The classic Royal chocolate entremet of almond succès sponge, praline feuilletine crunch and dark chocolate mousse, finished with a mirror-glaze dark coating.
ingredients: Succès sponge: 180 g egg whites, 46 g caster sugar, 180 g almond powder, 136 g icing sugar, 36 g potato starch
Praline crunch: 37.5 g milk chocolate (Lactee superieure 38%), 150 g 50% almond/hazelnut praliné, 75 g feuilletine
Chocolate mousse: 125 g syrup at 60 Bx, 142 g egg yolks, 250 g Extra Bitter Guayakil 64% dark chocolate, 500 g cream (35%)
Dark glaze: 12 g gelatin powder, 72 g water, 100 g water, 250 g caster sugar, 200 g cream (35%), 74 g glucose syrup DE38, 80 g cocoa powder
Assembly and finishing: 300 g milk chocolate (Lactee superieure 38%) for decorations
instructions: Succès sponge: whip the egg whites with the caster sugar until stiff, fold in the sifted almond powder, icing sugar and potato starch, pipe two 16cm disks per entremet with a 10mm tip, dust with icing sugar, bake about 10 minutes at 180C, and trim to 14cm.
Praline crunch: melt the milk chocolate to 45C, mix in the praliné then the feuilletine, spread onto one succès disk per entremet, and freeze.

Chocolate mousse: melt the dark chocolate to 55C and whip the cream soft. Poach the yolks and 60 Bx syrup in a bain-marie to 65C (82C for fresh yolks) while whisking, then whip to a ribbon pate a bombe.
Whisk a third of the pate a bombe and a third of the whipped cream into the hot melted chocolate, gently add the remaining pate a bombe, then fold in the remaining whipped cream; use immediately.
Dark glaze: boil the 100 g water, sugar, cream and glucose, add sifted cocoa off heat, boil again 1 minute while whisking, off heat add rehydrated gelatin, strain and cool quickly.
Assembly: in a 16cm ring spread chocolate mousse up the sides, place a succès disk and cover with mousse, add the succès/praline crunch insert (crunch inward), smooth level and freeze.
Finishing: glaze the frozen entremet with tempered dark glaze (about 31-32C) and decorate with milk chocolate pieces.

title: Cake au Citron
description: A moist lemon loaf cake soaked in lemon syrup and finished with a glaze, snow sugar, and candied lemon peel.
ingredients: Syrup: 400 g water, 200 g caster sugar, 90 g lemon puree
Finishing: 100 g neutral hot glaze, 2 g decoration sugar, 2 lemons, 20 g candied lemon peel strips
instructions: Mix the eggs, sugar, salt and cream with the paddle.
Gradually add the sifted flour and baking powder, then mix.
Add the butter melted to 40C and the lemon zest, then mix.
Pour 400 g of batter per 18x6cm cake pan.
Using a papercone, pipe a line of softened butter down the center of each cake.
Bake 45 minutes at 150C.
Make a syrup with the water and sugar, then add the lemon puree.
Generously soak the hot cakes with a ladle, then film and refrigerate.
Glaze the cakes and decorate with snow sugar, lemon chips and candied lemon peel.

title: Cake Marbré
description: A marbled vanilla and chocolate loaf cake finished with a crunchy chocolate-almond coating.
ingredients: Vanilla batter: 90 g egg yolks, 123 g caster sugar, 66 g thick cream, 95 g pastry wheat flour T65, 2 g baking powder, 35 g butter, 2 g vanilla extract
Chocolate batter: 104 g egg yolks, 140 g caster sugar, 80 g thick cream, 93 g pastry wheat flour T65, 2.5 g baking powder, 43 g butter, 21 g cocoa powder
Crunchy coating: 500 g milk couverture 38%, 100 g cocoa butter, 100 g grapeseed oil, 100 g chopped almonds
instructions: For each batter, lightly blanch the yolks and sugar, then whisk in the thick cream.
Whisk in the sifted dry ingredients (flour and baking powder; add cocoa for the chocolate batter).
Add the melted butter (and vanilla for the vanilla batter) and mix until homogeneous.
For the coating, mix the chocolate and cocoa butter melted at 45C with the grapeseed oil and roasted chopped almonds; hold at 35C.
Pour 200 g vanilla batter and 200 g chocolate batter per 18x6cm pan and marble with a spatula.
Pipe a line of softened butter down the center of each cake.
Bake 50 minutes at 150C.
Glaze the cooled cakes with the crunchy coating.

title: Gianduja Cups
description: Molded dark chocolate cups piped with a whipped homemade hazelnut gianduja and topped with a roasted hazelnut.
instructions: Melt and temper the dark chocolate, mold the cups and crystallize at 17C.
Roast the 250 g hazelnuts 15 minutes at 150C and cool.
Blend the hazelnuts and icing sugar without exceeding 40C, add the cold chocolate and cocoa butter, and blend without exceeding 40C.
Temper the gianduja to 24C, store in an airtight container at 17C.
Lightly warm and whip the gianduja, pipe a rosette into each cup with a star tip.
Decorate each cup with a roasted half-hazelnut.

title: Chaussons aux Pommes
description: Classic puff pastry turnovers filled with spiced apple compote, egg-washed and baked until golden.
ingredients: Classic puff pastry: 500 g pastry wheat flour T65, 10 g salt, 80 g butter, 250 g water, 4 g white vinegar, 300 g dry butter
Apple compote: 4 Golden apples, 40 g caster sugar, 1 g vanilla powder, 1 g cinnamon powder
Shaping and baking: 50 g egg yolks, 50 g 30Bx syrup
instructions: Dissolve the salt and vinegar in the water, add the flour and soft butter, and knead briefly with the hook.
Roll the dough to 36x18cm and cool; roll the dry butter to 18x18cm.
Lock in the butter and give 2 simple folds, resting 1 hour in the fridge; repeat twice for 6 simple folds total, then rest 12 hours.
For the compote, dice the apples into brunoise and cook covered with the sugar (10% of the apple weight).
Once translucent, cook uncovered to dry the compote, then cool quickly.
Roll the dough to 4 mm and cut 11 cm disks, then roll to 2 mm to ovalize.
Eggwash the edges and place about 40 g of compote on the bottom of each oval, then fold, seal and crimp.
Rest in the fridge, turn over, eggwash twice with yolks and score.
Cut a chimney in the center and bake about 25 minutes at 180C.
Brush with syrup and dry a few minutes in the oven.

title: Galette Frangipane
description: An inverse puff pastry galette filled with a spiral of frangipane cream, egg-washed, scored, and baked golden.
ingredients: Inverse puff pastry - dough: 460 g pastry wheat flour T65, 12 g salt, 80 g butter, 200 g water, 4 g white vinegar
Inverse puff pastry - kneaded butter: 400 g dry butter, 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 100 g strong wheat flour
Frangipane cream - pastry cream: 125 g semi-skimmed milk, 15 g egg yolks, 25 g caster sugar, 7 g custard powder
Frangipane cream - almond cream: 85 g butter, 85 g almond powder, 85 g caster sugar, 85 g whole eggs
Shaping and baking: 50 g egg yolks, 50 g 60Bx syrup
instructions: Dissolve the salt and vinegar in the water, add the flour and soft butter, and knead briefly; roll to 17x34cm and cool.
Mix the dry butter with both flours until homogeneous, roll to 17x51cm and cool.
Lock the dough into the kneaded butter and give a double fold then a single fold; rest 1 hour, repeat, then rest 12 hours.
For the pastry cream, warm the milk, blanch yolks and sugar with the custard powder, add the hot milk, cook until the starch slackens, then cool quickly.
For the almond cream, mix softened butter, sugar and almond powder, then add the eggs little by little; cool quickly.
Warm and smooth both creams and mix them together; use immediately.
Roll half the dough to 3 mm and half to 2 mm, cutting a 24x24cm square each.
Pipe a 16 cm spiral of frangipane on the 3 mm sheet, moisten the edges, cover with the 2 mm sheet and seal.
Cut a 22 cm disk, crimp, and rest in the fridge.
Turn over, eggwash twice with yolks, score, pierce chimneys, and bake about 45 minutes at 170C.
Brush with syrup and dry a few minutes in the oven.

title: Millefeuille Moderne
description: A modern millefeuille of caramelized rough puff pastry layered with vanilla mousseline cream and topped with piped gelified chantilly.
ingredients: Rough puff pastry: 250 g pastry wheat flour T65, 5 g salt, 125 g water, 2 g white vinegar, 200 g dry butter
Shaping and baking: 50 g icing sugar
Vanilla mousseline cream: 500 g semi-skimmed milk, 0.5 vanilla pod, 60 g egg yolks, 100 g caster sugar, 40 g custard powder, 280 g butter
Gelified chantilly cream: 3 g gelatin powder, 18 g water, 400 g cream 35%, 40 g caster sugar, 1 g vanilla powder
instructions: Dissolve the salt and vinegar in the water, add the flour and cold folding butter, and knead briefly.
Roll rectangular, rest 10 minutes, give a simple fold, and repeat until 5 simple folds are done.
Roll to 2.5 mm in a 40x45cm rectangle, prick all over and dust both sides with icing sugar.
Bake covered with a sheet about 35 minutes at 180C, then cut 3 strips of 12x40cm while hot.
Cook the milk, vanilla, yolks, sugar and custard powder like a pastry cream, cool quickly, then whisk smooth.
Whip the butter until light and add the smooth pastry cream in two additions; use immediately.
For the chantilly, bring a third of the cream with sugar and vanilla to a simmer, add rehydrated gelatin, add the rest of the cream and blend; rest 12 hours.
Pipe mousseline on 2 of the 3 strips using a 10 mm tip, stack the 3 strips, and cut 10 pieces 4 cm wide.
Stand them on the side, whip the gelified chantilly and pipe a zigzag with a Saint Honore tip on each.
Dust with vanilla powder.

title: Exotic Soft Caramel
description: Soft cut caramels flavored with passion fruit and mango, studded with roasted almonds and wrapped individually.
instructions: Cook the fruit purees, vanilla, cream, sugar and glucose to 123C.
Test the consistency, add the butter and stir in the roasted chopped almonds.
Immediately pour into a greased 20x20cm frame and cool away from moisture.
Cut into 4x1cm rectangles and wrap individually in caramel wrappers.

title: Pithiviers
description: An inverse puff pastry pie filled with a spiral of almond cream, festooned edges, and a rosette-scored top.
ingredients: Inverse puff pastry - dough: 460 g pastry wheat flour T65, 12 g salt, 80 g butter, 200 g water, 4 g white vinegar
Inverse puff pastry - kneaded butter: 400 g dry butter, 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 100 g strong wheat flour
Almond cream: 100 g butter, 100 g almond powder, 100 g caster sugar, 100 g whole eggs
Shaping and baking: 50 g egg yolks, 50 g 60Bx syrup
instructions: Dissolve the salt and vinegar in the water, add the flour and soft butter, and knead briefly; roll to 17x34cm and cool.
Mix the dry butter with both flours until homogeneous, roll to 17x51cm and cool.
Lock the dough into the kneaded butter and give a double fold then a single fold; rest 1 hour, repeat, then rest 12 hours.
Mix softened butter, sugar and almond powder, then add the eggs little by little; use immediately.
Roll half the dough to 3 mm and half to 2 mm, cutting a 24x24cm square each.
Pipe a 16 cm spiral of almond cream on the 3 mm sheet, moisten the edges, cover with the 2 mm sheet and seal.
Set briefly in the freezer, then festoon the edges with a tip; rest in the fridge.
Turn over, eggwash twice with yolks, score in a rosette, pierce chimneys, and bake about 45 minutes at 170C.
Brush with syrup and dry a few minutes in the oven.

title: Tarte Feuilletée aux Pommes
description: A classic puff pastry apple tart layered with apple compote and a rosette of thin apple slices, glazed after baking.
ingredients: Classic puff pastry: 250 g pastry wheat flour T65, 5 g salt, 40 g butter, 125 g water, 2 g white vinegar, 150 g dry butter
Apple compote: 1 Golden apple, 40 g caster sugar, 1 g vanilla powder
Shaping and baking: 25 g caster sugar, 25 g butter, 200 g neutral hot glaze, 4 g decoration sugar
instructions: Dissolve the salt and vinegar in the water, add the flour and soft butter, and knead briefly.
Roll the dough to 30x15cm and cool; roll the dry butter to 15x15cm.
Lock in the butter and give 2 simple folds, resting 1 hour; repeat twice for 6 simple folds, then rest 12 hours.
For the compote, dice 1 apple, cook covered with the sugar (10% of the apple weight), then dry uncovered and cool quickly.
Finely slice the remaining apples to 1 mm and use immediately.
Roll the dough to 2 mm, cut an 18 cm disk per tart, and fold the edges to form a rim.
Spread the compote in the base and arrange the apple slices in an overlapping rosette.
Butter and sprinkle with sugar, then bake 25 minutes at 160C.
Once cooled, glaze the tarts and dust the edges with snow sugar.

title: Pain au Chocolat
description: Leavened laminated pastry rolled around two chocolate batons for a flaky, buttery pain au chocolat.
ingredients: Leavened laminated dough: 150 g pastry wheat flour T65, 150 g strong wheat flour, 6 g salt, 45 g caster sugar, 15 g fresh yeast, 145 g semi-skimmed milk, 30 g fermented dough, 60 g butter
Baking: 35 g egg yolks, 15 g semi-skimmed milk
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, add flours, salt, sugar, fermented dough and tempered butter, then knead 5 minutes on speed 1 and 5 minutes on speed 2 (end temperature 24C).
First proof 30-45 minutes at room temperature then chill (or 10 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Roll the dough to 24x20 cm, roll the folding butter to 12x20 cm, enclose it and give one double and one single fold, then rest 1 hour in the fridge.
Roll into a 28x40 cm rectangle 3.5 mm thick, cut ten 14x8 cm rectangles and roll each around 2 chocolate sticks.
Proof 2h30 at 26C.
Eggwash with the yolk-milk mix and bake 17 minutes at 160C in a fan oven (or 17 minutes at 190C in a deck oven).

title: Pain aux Raisins
description: Spiral laminated pastries rolled with vanilla pastry cream and rum-soaked raisins, glazed after baking.
ingredients: Pastry cream: 200 g whole milk, 24 g egg yolks, 40 g caster sugar, 10 g custard powder, 10 g pastry wheat flour T65, 1 g vanilla powder
Rum raisins: 150 g blond raisins, 30 g water, 10 g brown rum

Leavened laminated dough: 150 g pastry wheat flour T65, 150 g strong wheat flour, 6 g salt, 45 g caster sugar, 15 g fresh yeast, 145 g semi-skimmed milk, 30 g fermented dough, 60 g butter, 150 g dry (folding) butter
Baking: 35 g egg yolks, 15 g semi-skimmed milk
instructions: Make the pastry cream: heat milk with vanilla, blanch yolks and sugar, mix in custard powder and flour, temper with hot milk, cook until the starch slackens and cool quickly.
Soak the raisins in warm water and rum overnight at room temperature.

For the dough, dissolve the yeast in the milk, add flours, salt, sugar, fermented dough and tempered butter, knead 5 minutes on speed 1 and 5 minutes on speed 2 (24C), then proof 30-45 minutes and chill (or 10 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Roll to 24x20 cm, laminate with the 12x20 cm butter block giving one double and one single fold, then rest 1 hour in the fridge.
Roll into a 30x40 cm rectangle 3.5 mm thick, spread with smoothed pastry cream, scatter drained raisins, roll tightly into a 30 cm cylinder and cut twelve 2.5 cm slices.
Proof 2h30 at 26C, eggwash and bake 17 minutes at 160C in a fan oven (or 17 minutes at 190C in a deck oven), then glaze with 30B syrup and return 1 minute to the oven.

title: Pain Chocolat Praline Bicolore
description: Two-tone laminated pastry pairing a cocoa leavened dough with plain dough, rolled around a chocolate baton and a homemade praline stick.
ingredients: Old-style praline: 20 g whole almonds, 20 g skinned hazelnuts, 40 g caster sugar, 15 g water
Chocolate leavened dough: 27 g pastry wheat flour T65, 27 g strong wheat flour, 6 g cocoa powder, 1 g salt, 9 g caster sugar, 3 g fresh yeast, 32 g semi-skimmed milk, 12 g butter, 6 g fermented dough

Leavened laminated dough: 150 g pastry wheat flour T65, 150 g strong wheat flour, 6 g salt, 45 g caster sugar, 15 g fresh yeast, 145 g semi-skimmed milk, 60 g butter, 150 g dry (folding) butter, 30 g fermented dough
Finishing: 29 g caster sugar, 21 g water
instructions: Make the praline: roast the nuts 15 minutes at 150C, cook water and sugar to a brown caramel, stir in the nuts, cool on a silicone mat, blend coarsely, roll into an 8x12 cm slab, freeze and cut twelve 1 cm sticks.
Make the cocoa leavened dough by dissolving yeast in milk and kneading with flours, cocoa, salt, sugar, fermented dough and butter (24C), then chill at 4C.
Make the plain laminated dough the same way, proof 30-45 minutes and chill, then laminate with the folding butter giving one double and one single fold and rest 1 hour.
Roll the chocolate dough to the same size, moisten and stick it onto the plain dough, then roll the assembly into a 28x48 cm rectangle 3.5 mm thick and cut twelve 8x14 cm rectangles.
Score the chocolate face of each, turn over, place a chocolate stick and a praline stick and roll up.
Proof 2h30 at 26C, eggwash and bake 17 minutes at 160C in a fan oven (or 17 minutes at 190C in a deck oven), then brush with syrup and dry 1 minute in the oven.

title: Tropezienne
description: A crumble-topped brioche disc split and filled generously with vanilla diplomate cream, finished with icing sugar.
ingredients: Crumble: 40 g butter, 40 g caster sugar, 40 g pastry wheat flour T65, 40 g almond powder
Brioche dough: 150 g pastry wheat flour T65, 150 g strong wheat flour, 6 g salt, 36 g caster sugar, 15 g fresh yeast, 180 g whole eggs, 150 g butter
Baking: 50 g whole eggs, 160 g crumble, 100 g pearl sugar
Vanilla diplomate cream: 390 g semi-skimmed milk, 1 vanilla pod, 130 g egg yolks, 143 g caster sugar, 31 g custard powder, 8 g gelatin powder, 48 g water, 390 g liquid cream 35%
instructions: Make the crumble by sanding butter with sugar, flour and almond powder, sieve and chill.
For the brioche, dissolve yeast in the eggs, add flours, salt and sugar, knead 3 minutes on speed 1 then 5-6 minutes on speed 2, add cold butter gradually and knead until it comes off the bowl (25C).
First proof 1 hour at room temperature then chill (or 30-40 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Roll the cold dough to 8 mm, relax in the fridge and cut two 18 cm discs; proof 1h30 at 26C.
Eggwash, sprinkle with raw crumble and pearl sugar and bake 15-20 minutes at 150C in a fan oven.
Make the diplomate cream: cook a vanilla pastry cream, stir in rehydrated gelatin, cool and smooth, then fold in the softly whipped cream in three additions.
Split the brioches horizontally, pipe teardrops of diplomate cream around the edge and a spiral inside with a 14 mm round tip, close and dust with icing sugar.

title: Carré Noisette
description: École Ducasse hazelnut fingers layering chocolate pain de Gênes, praliné crunch, hazelnut cream and diplomat cream, coated in almond glaze and topped with hazelnut Chantilly.
ingredients: Chocolate pain de Gênes: 74 g 50% almond paste, 77 g whole eggs, 8 g pastry wheat flour T65, 2 g cocoa powder, 1 g baking powder, 24 g butter, 8 g Extra Bitter Guayakil 64%. Crunch: 16 g butter, 40 g milk chocolate (Lactee superieure 38%), 56 g hazelnut paste, 100 g 50% almond/hazelnut praliné, 55 g puffed rice. Hazelnut cream: 94 g cream 35%, 37 g semi-skimmed milk, 30 g egg yolks, 142 g milk gianduja, 17 g Extra Bitter Guayakil 64%. Praliné diplomat cream: 2 g gelatin powder, 12 g water, 91 g semi-skimmed milk, 14 g caster sugar, 10 g egg yolks, 8 g custard powder, 120 g 50% almond/hazelnut praliné, 370 g cream 35%. Crunchy almond coating: 108 g chopped almonds, 500 g milk chocolate 38%, 48 g Extra Bitter Guayakil 64%, 52 g grapeseed oil. Hazelnut Chantilly: 340 g cream 35%, 30 g caster sugar, 30 g hazelnut paste. Finishing: 300 g Extra Bitter Guayakil 64%, 20 g whole hazelnuts.
instructions: 1. Pain de Gênes: whip the tempered almond paste with the eggs; gently fold in sifted flour, cocoa and baking powder; add butter and chocolate melted at 45C; smooth into a 20x20cm frame and bake 6-8 min at 170C. 2. Crunch: mix chocolate and butter melted at 45C with hazelnut paste, praliné and puffed rice; spread over the sponge and freeze. 3. Hazelnut cream: heat cream and milk, temper the yolks, cook to 84C, pour over the gianduja and chocolate and emulsify; pour over the crunch and freeze. 4. Diplomat cream: heat milk, blanch yolks with sugar and custard powder, cook until the starch slackens, add rehydrated gelatin, cool to 40C and add praliné, cool to 30C, fold in cream whipped to soft texture in 3 additions; smooth over the hazelnut cream and freeze. 5. Almond coating: mix chocolates melted at 45C with grapeseed oil and roasted chopped almonds; hold at 35C. 6. Chantilly: whip cream with sugar added gradually to soft peaks, add hazelnut paste and finish to Chantilly. 7. Finishing: cut into 3x10cm fingers, dip in the 35C almond coating, pipe hazelnut Chantilly, and decorate with tempered dark chocolate decorations and crushed hazelnuts.

title: Macaron Cassis
description: Vegan blackcurrant macarons with aquafaba-style plant-protein shells sandwiching a blackcurrant and raspberry-chocolate cremeux.
ingredients: Shell blancs mix: 115 g water, 10.5 g potato protein, 0.5 g xanthan gum. Shells: 150 g almond powder, 150 g icing sugar, red food coloring (QS), 55 g blancs mix; Italian syrup: 50 g water, 150 g caster sugar; meringue: 55 g blancs mix, 15 g caster sugar, 1 g cream of tartar. Blackcurrant cremeux: 75 g water, 188 g blackcurrant puree, 5 g NH pectin, 4 g Natur emul, 75 g caster sugar, 7 g inulin, 12.5 g Inspiration Framboise, 58 g coconut oil.
instructions: 1. Blend the potato protein and xanthan gum into the water for the blancs mix. 2. Shells: blend the almond powder and icing sugar; whip 55 g blancs mix with the cream of tartar to maximum, pour the sugar syrup cooked to 118C over it; combine the other half of blancs mix with the powders for the macaronade, then gently fold in the warm meringue. 3. Pipe 3cm macarons with an 8mm plain tip onto a Silpat, tap the tray and bake about 14 min at 140C. 4. Cremeux: heat water and blackcurrant puree to 40C, add sugar, NH pectin and Natur emul and blend, heat to 85C, then add cocoa butter and coconut oil, blend and chill. 5. Pipe a drop of blackcurrant cremeux with a 10mm plain tip onto half the shells and sandwich with the remaining shells.

title: Pomme & Nuts (entremet)
description: A hazelnut-sponge entremet with praliné crunch, Calvados-spiked green apple compote and a gianduja mousse, sprayed with chocolate velvet.
ingredients: Hazelnut sponge: 20 g butter, 20 g hazelnut paste, 20 g invert sugar, 34 g caster sugar, 20 g almond powder, 34 g pastry wheat flour T65, 2 g baking powder, 34 g cream 35%, 68 g whole eggs. Praliné crunch: 20 g Jivara 40%, 130 g 50% almond/hazelnut praliné, 60 g feuilletine. Green apple compote: 5 Granny apples, 15 g water, 35 g Calvados, 50 g caster sugar, 6 g NH pectin, 1 vanilla pod. Gianduja mousse: 4 g gelatin powder, 24 g water, 150 g semi-skimmed milk, 230 g milk gianduja, 300 g cream 35%. Spray mixture: 100 g cocoa butter, 160 g Jivara 40%. Finishing: 50 g neutral glaze, 50 g 50% almond/hazelnut praliné, 50 g skinned hazelnuts, Granny apple.
instructions: 1. Sponge: briefly mix the cream with the sifted dry ingredients, add the eggs, then the butter, hazelnut paste and invert sugar melted at 40C; pour into two 14cm rings and bake 5-6 min at 170C. 2. Crunch: mix chocolate melted at 45C with praliné and feuilletine, spread over the sponge and freeze. 3. Compote: simmer the fine-diced apples with water and scraped vanilla until translucent, cool to 40C, add sugar and NH pectin, boil 1 min, add Calvados, set in two 14cm rings and freeze. 4. Mousse: bring milk to a simmer, add rehydrated gelatin, pour over the gianduja and emulsify, cool to 29C and fold in softly whipped cream. 5. Spray mixture: melt cocoa butter and milk chocolate, use at 35C. 6. Assembly: fill a 16cm ring halfway with mousse, add compote and more mousse, add the crunch/sponge insert, freeze, spray, and decorate with praliné-glaze lines, apple slices and roasted hazelnuts.

title: Tarte Citron Thym
description: Vegan individual lemon-thyme tarts with a coconut-oil shortbread, plant-protein dacquoise, lemon cremeux, lemon-thyme gel and torched thyme meringue.
ingredients: Coconut-oil shortbread: 2 g lecithin, 86 g coconut oil, 180 g pastry wheat flour T65, 26 g potato starch, 3 g guar gum, 84 g icing sugar, 34 g almond powder, 2 g salt, 80 g water. Dacquoise blancs mix: 58 g water, 6 g potato protein, 0.2 g xanthan gum, 0.3 g cream of tartar; then 63 g blancs mix, 43 g caster sugar, 0.3 g guar gum, 25 g icing sugar, 20 g almond powder, 13 g pastry wheat flour T65. Lemon cremeux: 180 g lemon puree, 24 g mango puree, 192 g water, 108 g caster sugar, 14 g NH pectin, 6 g Natur emul, 18 g inulin, 2.5 lemons (zest), 84 g coconut oil. Lemon-thyme gel: 80 g lime puree, 40 g water, 0.5 lime, 5 g lemon thyme, 20 g caster sugar, 1.5 g agar agar. Thyme meringue: 15 g lemon thyme, 60 g water, 2 g potato protein, 1 g pea protein, 0.1 g xanthan gum, 0.3 g salt, 0.5 g cream of tartar, 120 g caster sugar, 0.25 vanilla bean. Candied lemon: lemon, 400 g water, 300 g caster sugar.
instructions: 1. Shortbread: mix coconut oil and lecithin at 25C until smooth, add dry ingredients and sand, add water to form a dough, roll to 3mm and freeze, line oiled perforated rings, freeze blind and bake at 155C. 2. Dacquoise: blend the protein base, whip the blancs mix with sugar and guar gum, fold in sifted powders, pipe 7cm discs, dust and bake about 12 min at 180C. 3. Lemon cremeux: heat purees and water to 40C, add powders and blend, boil, add lemon zest, cool to 40C, add coconut oil, blend and chill. 4. Gel: infuse lemon thyme in water and lemon puree 30 min, strain, add sugar and agar at 40C, boil, blend and chill. 5. Meringue: dry the thyme to powder, blend the protein base, whip the blancs mix with sugar added gradually, then add vanilla and thyme powder. 6. Candied lemon: blanch lemon segments 3 times, cook covered in syrup 2-3 h until soft. 7. Assembly: place a dacquoise disc in each tart, smooth cremeux level, pipe and torch the meringue, pipe the gel and finish with candied lemon and thyme sprigs.

title: Tête de Linotte
description: A milk-chocolate entremet built on sweet pastry and pecan brownie with a salted caramel cremeux, milk chocolate mousse and mirror glaze.
ingredients: Sweet pastry: 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 60 g butter, 40 g icing sugar, 1 g salt, 8 g almond powder, 20 g whole eggs. Brownie: 52 g butter, 1 g salt, 95 g caster sugar, 47 g whole eggs, 13 g Guanaja 70%, 26 g 100% cocoa paste, 38 g pastry wheat flour T65, 50 g pecan nuts. Caramel cremeux: 4 g gelatin powder, 24 g water, 240 g cream 35%, 60 g glucose syrup DE38, 120 g caster sugar, 72 g salted butter. Milk chocolate mousse: 3 g gelatin powder, 18 g water, 215 g Jivara 40%, 155 g semi-skimmed milk, 310 g cream 35%. Milk chocolate glaze: 15 g gelatin powder, 75 g water, 225 g Jivara 40%, 112 g water, 225 g glucose syrup DE38, 225 g caster sugar, 150 g unsweetened condensed milk. Finishing: 300 g Jivara 40%.
instructions: 1. Sweet pastry: sand the dry ingredients with the butter, add eggs, knead briefly, chill, roll to 2.5mm, cut 14cm discs (and small squares for decor), bake 15 min at 155C then eggwash and bake 5-10 min more. 2. Brownie: whisk eggs, sugar and salt, add sifted flour, then chocolate, cocoa paste and butter melted at 45C, add crushed pecans, spread over the baked pastry discs and bake 10-15 min at 170C. 3. Caramel cremeux: boil the cream, dry-caramelize sugar and glucose, deglaze with the hot cream, cook to 103C, add rehydrated gelatin, cool to 40C, blend in diced butter, pour over the brownie and freeze. 4. Mousse: simmer milk, add rehydrated gelatin, pour over chocolate and emulsify, cool to 25C, fold in softly whipped cream. 5. Glaze: boil water and sugar with glucose to 103C, add condensed milk, boil again, add gelatin, pour over chocolate, emulsify, cool to 30C. 6. Assembly: fill a 16cm ring halfway with mousse, add the cremeux/brownie/pastry insert, freeze, glaze at 30C and decorate with tempered milk chocolate and pastry squares.

title: Zestes d'Été
description: A summery entremet with lemon cake and crumble, strawberry confit and a lemon white-chocolate mousse under a red mirror glaze.
ingredients: Crumble: 25 g caster sugar, 25 g pastry wheat flour T65, 25 g almond powder, 25 g butter. Lemon cake: 23 g butter, 60 g pastry wheat flour T65, 1 g baking powder, 0.5 lemon (zest), 60 g whole eggs, 75 g caster sugar, 1 g salt, 33 g cream 35%. Strawberry confit: 12 g lemon puree, 60 g caster sugar, 4 g NH pectin, 350 g strawberry puree, 60 g glucose syrup DE38. Lemon Ivoire mousse: 6 g gelatin powder, 36 g water, 140 g semi-skimmed milk, 2 lemons (zest), 210 g Ivoire 35%, 17 g cocoa butter, 8.5 g lemon puree, 290 g cream 35%. Red glaze: 8 g gelatin powder, 40 g water, 80 g semi-skimmed milk, 200 g caster sugar, 160 g cream 35%, 110 g glucose syrup DE38, 14 g potato starch, 1 g red food coloring, 100 g Opalys. Finishing: 300 g Opalys, 1 g red food coloring, 500 g strawberries, 50 g neutral glaze, 50 g sugarpaste.
instructions: 1. Crumble: sand all ingredients with the butter until homogeneous, sieve and bake 15 min at 160C. 2. Lemon cake: mix eggs, sugar, salt and cream, add sifted flour and baking powder, then melted butter at 40C and lemon zest; divide into two 14cm rings, scatter pre-cooked crumble and bake 10-12 min at 180C. 3. Confit: heat strawberry puree and glucose to 40C, add sugar and NH pectin, boil 1 min, add lemon puree, set in two 14cm rings and freeze. 4. Mousse: simmer milk, add rehydrated gelatin, pour over white chocolate, cocoa butter and lemon zest, emulsify, add lemon puree, cool to 28C, fold in softly whipped cream. 5. Red glaze: heat milk, cream and glucose to 40C, add sugar and starch, boil 2 min, add gelatin, pour over chocolate, add coloring, blend and cool. 6. Assembly: fill a 16cm ring halfway with mousse, add confit and more mousse, add the lemon cake, freeze, glaze red, and finish with red chocolate rings, glazed strawberry quarters and sugarpaste daisies.

title: Baba Verveine Bouchon
description: Individual rum-baba-style cakes soaked in a verbena and citrus syrup, topped with mascarpone whipped cream and crystallized verbena leaves.
ingredients: Baba dough: 200 g strong wheat flour, 16 g semi-skimmed milk, 10 g honey, 8 g fresh yeast, 240 g whole eggs, 72 g butter, 2 g salt. Verbena poaching syrup: 250 g water, 125 g caster sugar, 80 g verbena liqueur, 5 g verbena, 16 g lemon puree, 1 lime. Mascarpone whipped cream: 150 g cream 35%, 15 g mascarpone, 1 vanilla pod, 18 g caster sugar. Crystallized verbena: 8 g verbena, 125 g caster sugar, 25 g egg whites.
instructions: Mix the butter with the flour and salt, then add one third of the eggs with the yeast, honey and milk and knead until elastic. Add the rest of the eggs gradually while keeping the elasticity, then leave to set 30 minutes at room temperature. Degas and pipe 20 g per bouchon mould, leave to rise at 25C until the dough reaches the rim, then bake at 165C for 15 to 20 minutes. For the syrup, boil the water with the verbena and lime zest and infuse 20 minutes, strain, re-weigh and add the sugar and lemon juice, boil, cool and add the verbena liqueur, then soak the babas in the syrup at 60C. Whip the cream, mascarpone, vanilla and sugar to a fromage-blanc texture. Brush each verbena leaf with egg white, dust with sugar and dry at 50C. To plate, halve a baba, pipe a spoon of whipped cream in the center and decorate with crystallized verbena leaves.

title: Citron, Algue Kombu et Estragon
description: A citrus plated dessert combining a tarragon pistou, citrus jelly, kombu-seaweed lemon condiment, candied citrus and kalamansi sorbet.
ingredients: Tarragon pistou: 20 g tarragon, 20 g skinned almonds, 15 g lemon puree, 120 g olive oil, 4 g fleur de sel, 1 g Timut pepper, 40 g ice. Citrus jelly: 250 g water, 100 g lemon puree, 40 g honey, 8 g gelatin powder, 46 g water, 1 lemon, 1 orange, 1 lime, 1 g Timut pepper. Kombu seaweed paste: 1 pkt kombu, 100 g water, 50 g caster sugar, 1 lemon. Condiment: 70 g yuzu puree, 3 lemons, 63 g caster sugar, 7 g caster sugar, 1.2 g NH pectin, 100 g kombu paste. Candied lemons and oranges: 5 lemons, 5 oranges, 150 g water, 300 g caster sugar. Kalamansi sorbet: 420 g water, 165 g powdered glucose, 245 g caster sugar, 4.5 g 64S stabilizer, 560 g kalamansi puree, 1.5 lemons, 142 g candied citrus. Finishing: 2 lemons, 2 oranges, 0.5 lime, 1 caviar lime, 1 bunch cress.
instructions: For the pistou, blanch the almonds 5 minutes from cold water, chop them fine with the tarragon, then blend with the remaining ingredients and reserve at 4C. For the jelly, heat the water, lemon juice and honey to 50C, add rehydrated gelatin, then at 20C add the citrus zests and Timut pepper and reserve at 4C. The day before, rehydrate 50 g kombu in cold water, blend finely, then reduce with water, sugar and lemon juice until dry. For the condiment, chop 70 g lemon segments, heat with the seaweed paste, lemon juice and first sugar to 40C, add the sugar/pectin mix and boil 1 minute. Candy the trimmed lemons and oranges by blanching 3 to 6 times then confiting in syrup below 70C over 2 to 3 days. For the sorbet, heat the water, add sugar, glucose and stabilizer at 45C, boil, pour over the kalamansi puree and zest, blend, mature 12 h at 4C, then churn with the chopped candied citrus. To finish, arrange all elements on the plate with a quenelle of kalamansi sorbet and garnish with caviar lime, lime zest and cress.

title: Citron Vanille
description: A lemon and vanilla plated dessert layering vanilla whipped ganache, lemon cream, lemon confit, almond streusel and a lemon-oat seasoning.
ingredients: Vanilla whipped ganache: 75 g white chocolate 35%, 3.5 g gelatin powder, 15.5 g water, 331 g cream 35%, 1 vanilla pod. Lemon cream: 120 g lemon puree, 3 g gelatin powder, 16 g water, 120 g whole eggs, 75 g caster sugar, 75 g butter. Lemon confit: 2 lemons, 18 g caster sugar, 20 g lemon puree. Almond lemon streusel: 36 g salted butter, 36 g brown sugar, 47 g almond powder, 36 g pastry flour T65, 0.5 lemon, 1 g fleur de sel. Crystallized almonds: 90 g whole almonds, 45 g caster sugar, 15 g water. Lemon seasoning: 180 g semi-skimmed milk, 18 g brown sugar, 32 g oatmeal, 10 g cornstarch, 1 lemon. Semi-candied lemons: 1 lemon, 200 g water, 150 g caster sugar, vanilla pod.
instructions: For the ganache, simmer the cream, infuse with vanilla, reheat and strain over the white chocolate and rehydrated gelatin, blend and reserve at 4C. For the lemon cream, rehydrate the gelatin, add the remaining ingredients except butter, boil until thickened, cool to 35C, add butter and blend. For the confit, blanch the lemon zests 3 times, simmer with sugar and juice about 45 minutes and blend. Sand all streusel ingredients, spread and bake 20 minutes at 160C. Roast the almonds, cook water and sugar to 115C, add almonds and sand, then coarsely chop. For the seasoning, roast the oats, add milk and sugar, boil 5 minutes, add cornstarch and lemon zest and cook until thick. Cut the lemons in 4, blanch 6 times and confit slowly in vanilla syrup for several hours. Whip the vanilla ganache, pipe and plate the dessert with all the elements.

title: Feuilles de Chocolat Noir et Crémeux Caramel
description: A composed chocolate plate stacking dark chocolate sheets, caramel cream, gianduja crunch, caramel chantilly and foam, served with cocoa nib sorbet.
ingredients: Dark chocolate sheets: 200 g Guanaja 70%. Caramel cream: 250 g cream 35%, 30 g caster sugar, 80 g cream 35%, 20 g egg yolks, 120 g Araguani 72%, 2 g gelatin powder, 12 g water. Gianduja crunch: 150 g pastry flour T65, 90 g butter, 60 g icing sugar, 12 g almond powder, 30 g whole eggs, 2 g salt, 180 g dark gianduja. Caramel chantilly: 85 g caster sugar, 300 g cream 35%, 3 g gelatin powder, 18 g water. Caramel foam: 80 g caster sugar, 20 g glucose syrup DE38, 20 g water, 50 g water, 40 g egg whites. Cocoa nib sorbet: 80 g cocoa nibs, 240 g Guanaja 70%, 70 g caster sugar, 70 g invert sugar, 550 g whole milk, 1 g 64S stabilizer. Finishing: 10 g cocoa nibs.
instructions: Temper dark chocolate, spread between guitar sheets and cut squares. For the caramel cream, make a dry caramel with the sugar, deglaze with hot cream, cook over yolks to 85C, add gelatin, pour over chopped Araguani, blend, fold in whipped cream at 45C, set in a frame, freeze and cut squares. Make a shortbread, bake at 160C, crumble into melted gianduja, spread and cut squares. For the chantilly, make caramel powder, boil part of the cream with gelatin and caramel, add the rest and rest overnight. For the foam, cook a caramel with water, sugar and glucose, deglaze, strain, siphon with egg whites and charge. For the sorbet, roast the nibs, infuse in boiled milk, add sugars and stabilizer, boil over chopped chocolate, blend, mature 12 h and churn. Stack crunch, caramel cream and chocolate sheets, pipe caramel chantilly and foam, and serve with a quenelle of cocoa nib sorbet.

title: Île Flottante
description: Poached vanilla meringue islands floating on vanilla crème anglaise, topped with a caramel disk and toasted sliced almonds.
ingredients: Caramel: 500 g caster sugar (batch for 24 plates). Meringues: 50 g egg whites, 20 g caster sugar, 1 g vanilla powder. Creme anglaise: 250 g semi-skimmed milk, 250 g cream 35%, 1 g vanilla powder, 100 g egg yolks, 50 g caster sugar. Finishing: 25 g sliced almonds.
instructions: For the caramel disks, cook the sugar to a light caramel, pour onto paper, cool and blend, then dust onto a silicone mat, melt briefly at 200C and cut 7 cm disks. Whip the egg whites with the sugar until stiff, add vanilla powder, fill greased 6 cm half-sphere molds and level, then bake in a water bath at 110C for 10 to 12 minutes until a knife comes out dry. For the crème anglaise, heat the milk, cream and vanilla, blanch the yolks and sugar, combine and cook to 84C, then cool quickly. Fill verrines 2/3 with crème anglaise, unmold a meringue on top, place a caramel disk and decorate with toasted sliced almonds.

title: Entremet Coco-Chocolat
description: A vegan coconut-chocolate entremet with coconut dacquoise, chocolate crumble crunch, dark chocolate cremeux, coconut mousse and a whipped coconut ganache.
ingredients: Coconut dacquoise blancs mix: 115 g water, 10.5 g potato protein, 0.3 g xanthan gum, 0.5 g cream of tartar; then 100 g blancs mix, 85 g caster sugar, 0.5 g guar gum, 50 g icing sugar, 40 g grated coconut, 25 g pastry wheat flour T65, plus 20 g icing sugar to dust. Chocolate crumble: 40 g coconut sugar, 20 g grated coconut, 42 g pastry wheat flour T65, 8 g cocoa powder, 0.3 g salt, 34 g coconut oil, 6 g water. Crunch: 120 g crumble, 30 g grated coconut, 52 g Guanaja 70%, 75 g almond/hazelnut praliné. Chocolate cremeux: 200 g Guanaja 70%, 15 g coconut oil, 309 g water, 27 g inverted sugar, 4.2 g Natur emul. Coconut mousse blancs mix: 104 g water, 3.6 g pea protein, 0.26 g xanthan gum; then 585 g coconut puree, 15 g caster sugar, 11 g pectin 325 NH 95, 26 g Malibu, 1.3 g calcium lactate, 39 g caster sugar, 15.6 g inulin. Whipped ganache: 216 g coconut puree, 22 g caster sugar, 0.5 vanilla bean, 22 g cocoa butter, 32 g neutral coconut oil, 3.78 g pectin 325 NH 95, 0.5 lime. Finishing: 300 g Extra Bitter 61%, 150 g neutral glaze, coconut.
instructions: 1. Dacquoise: blend the potato protein, xanthan and cream of tartar into the water; whip the blancs mix with sugar and guar gum, fold in the sifted powders, pipe 14cm discs, dust with icing sugar and bake at 180C for about 12 min. 2. Crumble: sand all ingredients with the coconut oil, add water and bake at 160C. 3. Crunch: mix the cooked crumble with roasted coconut, add melted Guanaja with the praliné then the remaining chopped chocolate, spread on a dacquoise and reserve in the freezer. 4. Cremeux: melt coconut oil and chocolate at 45C, blend water and inverted sugar warmed to 40C with the Natur emul, combine; pour 230g over the dacquoise/crunch, top with the second dacquoise and freeze the insert. 5. Mousse: blend the pea protein base, heat the coconut puree to 40C with pectin and sugar, boil, cool to 55C and add Malibu; whip the blancs mix with sugar, lactate and inulin, fold into the coconut base and use immediately. 6. Ganache: heat coconut puree, vanilla, cocoa butter and oil to 40C, add pectin and sugar, boil 1 min, chill 12h, then whip with lime zest. 7. Assembly: line a 16cm ring with coconut mousse, add the insert, freeze, spray/glaze, and pipe the whipped ganache with a St-Honore tip.

title: Praline Molded Bonbons
description: Molded dark chocolate half-sphere shells filled with a simple almond-hazelnut praline and sealed.
instructions: Melt and temper the dark chocolate, mold the half-spheres and crystallize at 17C.
Melt the cocoa butter at 40C, add the praline and mix well, temper to 24C and fill the shells 3/4 full.
Crystallize 24 hours at 17C.
Seal with tempered dark chocolate, set 1 hour at 17C and unmold.

title: Brioche Feuilletee
description: Laminated brioche folding cold butter into an enriched dough for a flaky, layered crumb, shaped as loaves or braided individuals.
ingredients: Laminated brioche: 200 g pastry wheat flour T65, 100 g strong wheat flour, 6 g salt, 30 g caster sugar, 10 g fresh yeast, 80 g whole eggs, 100 g butter, 120 g dry (folding) butter, 85 g semi-skimmed milk
Eggwash: 35 g egg yolks, 15 g semi-skimmed milk
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the eggs and milk, add flours, salt and sugar, and knead with the hook 3 minutes on speed 1 then 5-6 minutes on speed 2.
Add cold butter gradually and knead until the dough comes off the bowl (end temperature 25C).
First proof 30-40 minutes at room temperature then 12 hours at 4C.
Roll the dough to 24x18 cm, roll the folding butter to 12x18 cm, enclose the butter and give one single and one double fold, then rest 1 hour at 4C.
Roll into a 15x60 cm rectangle 5 mm thick; cut a 4x60 cm strip (about 250 g) and 4.5x12 cm strips (45-50 g each).
Fold the large strip zig-zag into a greased nanterre mold and braid the small ones in aluminum cups.
Proof 2 hours at 26C for the loaf, 1h30 for individuals; eggwash and bake individuals 10 minutes at 155C and the loaf 20 minutes at 150C in a fan oven.

title: Brioche aux Pepites
description: Soft enriched brioche rolls folded with chocolate drops, snipped open and finished with pearl sugar.
ingredients: Brioche dough: 110 g pastry wheat flour T65, 110 g strong wheat flour, 5 g salt, 24 g caster sugar, 11 g fresh yeast, 132 g whole eggs, 110 g butter
Baking: 50 g whole eggs, 50 g pearl sugar
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the eggs, add flours, salt and sugar, and knead with the hook 3 minutes on speed 1 then 5-6 minutes on speed 2 until a glutinous network forms.
Add cold butter gradually and knead until the dough comes off the bowl (end temperature 25C).
First proof 1 hour at room temperature then chill (or 30-40 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Roll 500 g of dough into a 10x50 cm rectangle, sprinkle with 100 g drops, give a single fold widthwise, cut into ten 60 g pieces every 5 cm and roll each into a ball.
Proof 2 hours at 26C.
Eggwash, snip each brioche into 6 with scissors, sprinkle the center with drops and the edges with pearl sugar, then bake 10 minutes at 150C in a fan oven.

title: Brioche a Tete
description: Classic two-ball brioche a tete of rich egg-and-butter dough baked in fluted molds.
ingredients: Brioche dough: 100 g pastry wheat flour T65, 100 g strong wheat flour, 4 g salt, 24 g caster sugar, 10 g fresh yeast, 120 g whole eggs, 100 g butter
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the eggs, add flours, salt and sugar, and knead with the hook 3 minutes on speed 1 then 5-6 minutes on speed 2 until a glutinous network forms.
Add cold butter gradually and knead until the dough comes off the bowl (end temperature 25C).
First proof 1 hour at room temperature then chill (or 30-40 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Shape small heads at 45 g (35 g body plus 10 g head) or a large head at 360 g (280 g plus 80 g).
Proof small heads 1h30 at 26C, the large head 2h30 at 26C.
Eggwash and bake in a fan oven: small heads 10 minutes at 160C; large head 10 minutes at 150C then 15 minutes at 135C.

title: Couronne
description: A large ring-shaped brioche crown snipped with scissors and studded with pearl sugar.
ingredients: Brioche dough: 264 g strong wheat flour, 5 g salt, 30 g caster sugar, 13 g fresh yeast, 159 g whole eggs, 132 g butter
Baking: 50 g whole eggs, 50 g pearl sugar
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the eggs, add flour, salt and sugar, and knead with the hook 3 minutes on speed 1 then 5-6 minutes on speed 2 until a glutinous network forms.
Add cold butter gradually and knead until the dough comes off the bowl (end temperature 25C).
First proof 1 hour at room temperature then chill (or 30-40 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Shape into 300 g pieces formed as crowns and proof 2 hours at 26C.
Eggwash, snip the crowns with scissors and sprinkle with pearl sugar.
Bake in a fan oven 10 minutes at 150C then 10 minutes at 135C.

title: Croissant
description: Classic leavened laminated croissants made by folding a butter block into yeasted dough and rolling triangles.
ingredients: Leavened laminated dough: 150 g pastry wheat flour T65, 150 g strong wheat flour, 6 g salt, 45 g caster sugar, 15 g fresh yeast, 145 g semi-skimmed milk, 30 g fermented dough, 60 g butter
Baking: 35 g egg yolks, 15 g semi-skimmed milk
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, add flours, salt, sugar, fermented dough and tempered butter, then knead 5 minutes on speed 1 and 6-7 minutes on speed 2 (end temperature 24C).
First proof 30-45 minutes at room temperature then chill (or 10 minutes then 12 hours at 4C).
Roll the dough to 24x20 cm, roll the folding butter to 12x20 cm, enclose it and give one double and one single fold, then rest 1 hour in the fridge.
Roll into a 30x45 cm rectangle 3 mm thick, cut ten triangles with a 9 cm base (65-70 g each) and roll into croissants.
Proof 2h30 at 26C.
Eggwash with the yolk-milk mix and bake 17 minutes at 160C in a fan oven (or 17 minutes at 190C in a deck oven).

title: Oranges Givrées (Frosted Oranges)
description: Hollowed half-candied orange shells filled with orange sorbet and capped, a classic frozen fruit dessert.
instructions: Orange sorbet: heat the water and milk powder; at 30C add the sugar (reserving a little) and glucose and mix well.
At 45C add the stabilizer premixed with the reserved sugar; cook to 85C and blend.
Cool quickly to 4C, mature 12 hours, add the orange juice, blend again, churn and hold at -18C.
Half-candied oranges: cut the top off each orange about 1cm down and scoop them out completely.
Bring the water and sugar to a simmer, off the heat add the peels and candy 12 hours at room temperature; drain, shape on a sheet and freeze.
Fill 4cm half-spheres with orange sorbet, smooth flush and freeze.
Fill the orange shells with sorbet, smooth flush, set a half-sphere on each and close with the peel cap.

title: Crème Brûlée
description: Classic slow-baked vanilla custard finished with a caramelized brown-sugar crust.
ingredients: Custard: 585 g cream 35%, 97 g semi-skimmed milk, 156 g egg yolks, 65 g caster sugar, 1 g vanilla powder. Finishing: 100 g brown sugar.
instructions: Blanch the yolks and sugar, then add the milk, vanilla and cream and mix well. Divide the mixture into 4 ramekins, filling them 4/5 full. Bake about 1 hour at 90C until the creams are slightly wobbly, then cool quickly. Sprinkle with brown sugar, remove the excess and caramelize with a blowtorch, optionally caramelizing a second time.

title: Mont-Blanc Mandarine
description: A mandarin twist on the Mont-Blanc with shortbread, vanilla whipped ganache cones, piped chestnut cream, chestnut panna cotta and mandarin confit.
ingredients: Shortbread: 60 g butter, 38 g icing sugar, 12 g almond powder, 0.5 g salt, 1 g vanilla powder, 95 g pastry flour T65, 20 g egg yolks. French meringue: 35 g egg whites, 35 g caster sugar, 25 g icing sugar. Vanilla whipped ganache: 6 g water, 1 g gelatin powder, 0.5 vanilla pod, 60 g white chocolate 35%, 250 g cream 35%. Chestnut cream: 125 g chestnut paste, 63 g chestnut cream, 30 g butter, 2 g whisky. Mandarin confit: 125 g mandarin puree, 1 mandarin, 25 g caster sugar, 2 g NH pectin. Chestnut panna cotta: 18 g water, 3 g gelatin powder, 375 g cream 35%, 60 g caster sugar, 113 g chestnut paste, 7 g whisky. Finishing: 4 mandarins, 6 candied chestnuts, 10 g decoration sugar.
instructions: Sand the dry shortbread ingredients with butter, add the yolks, knead briefly, roll to 2 mm, cut discs and bake 12 to 15 minutes at 160C. Whip the egg whites with caster sugar, fold in icing sugar, pipe and bake at 90C for several hours. For the ganache, boil part of the cream with vanilla, add gelatin, strain over white chocolate, blend with the cold cream and rest 12 h, then whip, mold into cones with a meringue center and freeze. Mix the chestnut paste with chestnut cream, add softened butter and whisky and whip. Heat the mandarin puree with zest to 40C, add the sugar/pectin mix and boil. For the panna cotta, boil the cream and sugar, add gelatin, blend in the chestnut paste and whisky. To finish, layer mandarin segments, panna cotta and confit in verrines, set an unmolded ganache cone on a shortbread disc, pipe chestnut cream, dust with sugar and top with a candied chestnut and meringues.

title: Soufflé au Chocolat
description: Individual hot chocolate soufflés baked in brown-sugar-lined molds and dusted with icing sugar.
ingredients: 126 g Caraibe 66%, 120 g semi-skimmed milk, 6 g cornstarch, 24 g egg yolks, 240 g egg whites, 36 g caster sugar, 25 g butter, 100 g brown sugar (for molds).
instructions: Heat the milk. Whisk the yolks and cornstarch, add some of the hot milk, mix, bring everything to a boil, then add the chocolate and blend. Whip the egg whites with the caster sugar until stiff and gently fold them into the chocolate base without deflating it. Fill buttered, brown-sugar-lined soufflé molds, level the tops, clean the rims with a thumb, and bake 10 to 12 minutes at 180C. Dust with icing sugar and serve immediately.

title: Mi-Cuit au Chocolat
description: Molten-centered chocolate sponge baked to order and served with a warm dark chocolate sauce.
ingredients: Molten chocolate sponge: 53 g pastry flour T65, 120 g butter, 127 g Guanaja 70%, 160 g caster sugar, 200 g whole eggs, 20 g butter (for molds). Chocolate sauce: 15 g butter, 120 g Extra Bitter Guayakil 64%, 130 g semi-skimmed milk, 70 g cream 35%.
instructions: Whip the eggs and sugar for about 10 minutes, add the butter and chocolate melted at 40C and mix gently, then fold in the sifted flour and rest in the fridge about 2 hours. Fill 4 buttered, paper-lined 6 cm rings halfway and bake 8 minutes at 210C, then plate immediately and remove the rings. For the sauce, simmer the milk and cream, pour over the chopped chocolate and emulsify, add the diced butter, blend and serve alongside the mi-cuits.
